description: Variation of sound speed in a gas with absolute temperature. \(v\)=speed at temperature \(T\) (in kelvin), \(v_0\)=speed at 273 K (~332 m/s for air), \(T\)=absolute temperature.

related_concepts.name: Speed in terms of Molar Mass
related_concepts.definition: \(v=\sqrt{\gamma RT/M}\): sound speed rises with temperature and falls with molar mass \(M\).

related_concepts.name: Approximation
related_concepts.definition: In air, \(v\) increases by about \(0.61\,\text{m/s}\) per \(^{\circ}\text{C}\) rise near room temperature.

subject: Physics
title: Speed of Sound (Molar Form)
description: Sound speed in an ideal gas from kinetic theory. \(\gamma\)=ratio of specific heats, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=absolute temperature, \(M\)=molar mass of gas.

related_concepts.name: Effect of Humidity
related_concepts.definition: Humid air is less dense, so sound travels faster than in dry air.

related_concepts.name: Independence of Pressure
related_concepts.definition: At constant temperature \(v\) is independent of pressure (since \(P/\rho\) is constant).

subject: Physics
title: Sound Wave: Pressure Amplitude
visual_data: \Delta P = \Delta P_0 \cos(kx - \omega t), \quad \Delta P_0 = B A k = \rho v \omega A
description: Pressure variation in a longitudinal sound wave; leads displacement by \(\pi/2\). \(\Delta P_0\)=pressure amplitude, \(B\)=bulk modulus, \(A\)=displacement amplitude, \(k\)=wave number, \(\rho\)=density, \(v\)=sound speed, \(\omega\)=angular frequency.

related_concepts.name: Phase Difference
related_concepts.definition: Pressure wave and displacement wave are \(\pi/2\) (90°) out of phase: displacement node = pressure antinode.

related_concepts.name: Bulk Modulus Link
related_concepts.definition: \(v=\sqrt{B/\rho}\) for a fluid medium.

subject: Physics
title: Intensity of Sound Wave
description: Average energy flux per unit area carried by a sound wave. \(I\)=intensity, \(\rho\)=density, \(v\)=sound speed, \(\omega\)=angular frequency, \(A\)=displacement amplitude, \(\Delta P_0\)=pressure amplitude.

related_concepts.name: Intensity–Amplitude
related_concepts.definition: \(I\propto A^2\) and \(I\propto f^2\): intensity scales with square of amplitude and frequency.

related_concepts.name: Threshold Intensity
related_concepts.definition: \(I_0=10^{-12}\,\text{W/m}^2\) is the reference intensity of hearing.

subject: Physics
title: String: Frequency of nth Harmonic
description: Resonant frequencies of a string fixed at both ends (all harmonics present). \(n\)=harmonic number, \(L\)=length, \(T\)=tension, \(\mu\)=mass per unit length.

related_concepts.name: Fundamental
related_concepts.definition: \(n=1\) gives the lowest frequency (first harmonic) \(f_1=\frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{T/\mu}\).

related_concepts.name: Number of Loops
related_concepts.definition: \(n\) equals the number of antinodes (loops) in the standing wave pattern.

subject: Physics
title: Law of Transverse Vibrations (Strings)
description: Three laws of vibrating strings for the fundamental frequency. \(f\)=frequency, \(L\)=length, \(T\)=tension, \(\mu\)=linear mass density.

related_concepts.name: Law of Length
related_concepts.definition: At constant T and \(\mu\), \(f\propto 1/L\) (the sonometer law).

related_concepts.name: Sonometer
related_concepts.definition: Apparatus to verify string laws by measuring resonant length for a given tuning fork.

subject: Physics
title: End Correction (Organ Pipe)
description: Correction added to pipe length due to antinode forming slightly outside the open end. \(e\)=end correction, \(r\)=pipe radius, \(L\)=physical length, \(L_{eff}\)=effective length.

related_concepts.name: Open Pipe Correction
related_concepts.definition: Both ends open add \(2e\); a closed pipe adds one \(e\) at the open end.

related_concepts.name: Resonance Tube Use
related_concepts.definition: \(v=2f(l_2-l_1)\) eliminates end correction by taking the difference of two resonance lengths.

subject: Physics
title: Harmonics in Organ Pipes
description: Which harmonics are present in pipes. Open pipe contains all integer harmonics; closed pipe contains only odd harmonics. \(n\)=integer harmonic index.

related_concepts.name: Fundamental Comparison
related_concepts.definition: For same length, open pipe fundamental \(=v/2L\) is twice the closed pipe fundamental \(=v/4L\).

related_concepts.name: Quality (Timbre)
related_concepts.definition: Richer harmonic content makes open pipes sound mellower than closed pipes.

subject: Physics
title: Beats: Unknown Fork Frequency
description: Determining an unknown frequency by loading/filing a fork to see if beats rise or fall. \(f_1\)=known frequency, \(f_2\)=unknown frequency, \(f_{beat}\)=beat frequency.

related_concepts.name: Wax Loading
related_concepts.definition: Adding wax lowers a fork's frequency; if beats decrease, the unknown was higher (use \(+\)).

related_concepts.name: Filing
related_concepts.definition: Filing a fork raises its frequency, the opposite effect of loading with wax.

subject: Physics
title: Reflection: Phase Change
description: Phase change on reflection of a wave. A wave reflecting from a rigid (denser) boundary inverts (\(\pi\) shift); from a free (rarer) boundary it does not. \(\Delta\phi\)=phase change.

related_concepts.name: Crest to Trough
related_concepts.definition: At a rigid boundary a crest reflects as a trough (half-wavelength path change).

related_concepts.name: Open Pipe End
related_concepts.definition: Sound reflecting at an open end (rarer) returns without inversion, forming a displacement antinode.

subject: Physics
title: Doppler: General 3-D Formula
description: Doppler shift when source/observer velocities make angles with the line joining them. \(f'\)=observed frequency, \(f_0\)=source frequency, \(v\)=sound speed, \(v_o,v_s\)=observer/source speeds, \(\theta_o,\theta_s\)=angles with line of sight.

related_concepts.name: Transverse Doppler
related_concepts.definition: When velocity is perpendicular to line of sight (\(\theta=90^\circ\)), the classical (sound) Doppler shift is zero.

related_concepts.name: Sign Convention
related_concepts.definition: Use velocity components along the source–observer line; only these cause a frequency shift.

subject: Physics
title: Two Identical Sources: Resultant Intensity
description: Intensity at a point from interference of two coherent sources of equal intensity \(I_0\). \(I\)=resultant intensity, \(\phi\)=phase difference, \(I_0\)=intensity of each source.

related_concepts.name: Constructive
related_concepts.definition: \(\phi=2n\pi\) gives \(I_{max}=4I_0\) (amplitudes add).

related_concepts.name: Destructive
related_concepts.definition: \(\phi=(2n+1)\pi\) gives \(I_{min}=0\) (amplitudes cancel).

subject: Physics
title: Path Difference & Phase Difference
description: Conversion between path difference and phase difference for interfering waves. \(\phi\)=phase difference, \(\Delta x\)=path difference, \(\lambda\)=wavelength.

related_concepts.name: Constructive Condition
related_concepts.definition: \(\Delta x=n\lambda\) (phase \(2n\pi\)) gives maximum amplitude.

related_concepts.name: Destructive Condition
related_concepts.definition: \(\Delta x=(2n-1)\lambda/2\) (phase odd multiple of \(\pi\)) gives minimum amplitude.

subject: Physics
title: Intensity Ratio & Amplitude
description: Maximum-to-minimum intensity ratio in interference of two waves. \(A_1,A_2\)=amplitudes, \(I_1,I_2\)=individual intensities, \(I_{max},I_{min}\)=extreme intensities.

related_concepts.name: Intensity–Amplitude
related_concepts.definition: \(I\propto A^2\), so amplitude ratio equals the square root of the intensity ratio.

related_concepts.name: Fringe Visibility
related_concepts.definition: \(V=(I_{max}-I_{min})/(I_{max}+I_{min})\); maximum when the two intensities are equal.

subject: Physics
title: Energy Density of a Wave
description: Average energy stored per unit volume by a mechanical wave. \(u\)=energy density, \(\rho\)=density of medium, \(\omega\)=angular frequency, \(A\)=amplitude.

related_concepts.name: Intensity Link
related_concepts.definition: \(I=u\,v\): intensity equals energy density times wave speed.

related_concepts.name: Energy Distribution
related_concepts.definition: Energy in a wave is split equally on average between kinetic and potential forms.

subject: Physics
title: Apparent Wavelength (Doppler)
description: Wavelength of sound altered by source motion (observer motion does not change \(\lambda\)). \(\lambda'\)=apparent wavelength, \(v\)=sound speed, \(v_s\)=source speed (\(-\) when approaching), \(f_0\)=source frequency.

related_concepts.name: Source Approaching
related_concepts.definition: Wavelength ahead of an approaching source is compressed (\(\lambda'<\lambda\)), raising pitch.

related_concepts.name: Observer Motion
related_concepts.definition: A moving observer changes the relative speed of sound, not the wavelength.

subject: Physics
title: Mirror Formula
description: Relation for spherical mirrors. \(v\): image, \(u\): object, \(f\): focal length.
derivation:
Derived using geometry of similar triangles formed by the object, image, and Center of Curvature (C).
For paraxial rays (small angles):
\(\tan \alpha \approx \alpha\).
Using exterior angle theorem and geometric relations:
\(\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{2}{R}\)
Since \(f = R/2\), we get:
\(\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}\)

related_concepts.name: Sign Convention
related_concepts.definition: Distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive; opposite are negative.

related_concepts.name: Paraxial Rays
related_concepts.definition: Rays close to the principal axis making small angles.

subject: Physics
title: Lens Formula
description: Thin lens equation.
derivation:
Consider a thin convex lens.
Triangles formed by the object and optical center are similar to those of the image and optical center.
\(\frac{h'}{h} = \frac{v}{u}\) (Magnification)
Using the focus, another set of similar triangles gives:
\(\frac{h'}{h} = \frac{v-f}{f}\)
Equating and simplifying yields:
\(\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}\)

related_concepts.name: Thin Lens Approximation
related_concepts.definition: Assumption that lens thickness is negligible compared to radii of curvature.

subject: Physics
title: Lens Maker's Formula
description: Focal length from geometry.
derivation:
Apply the refraction formula at a spherical surface twice.
Surface 1 (Air to Glass): \(\frac{\mu}{v_1} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{\mu-1}{R_1}\)
Surface 2 (Glass to Air): Image from surface 1 acts as object.
\(\frac{1}{v} - \frac{\mu}{v_1} = \frac{1-\mu}{R_2}\)
Adding both equations cancels \(\frac{\mu}{v_1}\):
\(\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = (\mu-1)(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2})\)
Since \(1/v - 1/u = 1/f\), the result follows.

related_concepts.name: Refractive Index
related_concepts.definition: Ratio of speed of light in vacuum to speed in the medium (\(n = c/v\)).

subject: Physics
title: Snell's Law
description: Refraction at interface.
derivation:
Derived from Fermat's Principle of Least Time.
Light takes the path that minimizes travel time.
\(t = \frac{d_1}{v_1} + \frac{d_2}{v_2} = \frac{d_1 n_1}{c} + \frac{d_2 n_2}{c}\)
Differentiating with respect to position on interface and setting to 0 yields:
\(n_1 \sin i = n_2 \sin r\)

related_concepts.name: Critical Angle
related_concepts.definition: Angle of incidence where angle of refraction is 90°, leading to Total Internal Reflection.

subject: Physics
title: Prism Formula
description: Refractive index of prism.
derivation:
For a prism, deviation \(\delta = (i + e) - A\).
At minimum deviation \(\delta_m\), the ray passes symmetrically:
\(i = e\) and \(r_1 = r_2 = r\).
From geometry, \(A = r_1 + r_2 = 2r \Rightarrow r = A/2\).
Also \(\delta_m = 2i - A \Rightarrow i = (A+\delta_m)/2\).
By Snell's Law \(\mu = \frac{\sin i}{\sin r}\), we get the formula.

related_concepts.name: Minimum Deviation
related_concepts.definition: The smallest angle of deviation, occurring when light travels parallel to the prism base.

subject: Physics
title: Simple Microscope (Near)
description: Magnifying power (Image at D).
derivation:
Object placed within focus ($u < f$).
Lens formula: $\frac{1}{-D} - \frac{1}{-u} = \frac{1}{f} \implies \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{D}$.
Magnification $m = \frac{v}{u} = \frac{D}{u}$.
$m = D(\frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{D}) = 1 + \frac{D}{f}$.

related_concepts.name: Near Point
related_concepts.definition: Closest distance for distinct vision (D = 25 cm for normal eye).

subject: Physics
title: Simple Microscope (Far)
description: Magnifying power (Image at Infinity).
derivation:
Object placed at focus ($u = f$).
Image forms at infinity (relaxed eye).
Angular magnification $\theta_i / \theta_o$.
$\theta_i \approx h/f$, $\theta_o \approx h/D$.
$MP = \frac{h/f}{h/D} = \frac{D}{f}$.

related_concepts.name: Angular Magnification
related_concepts.definition: Ratio of angle subtended by image to angle subtended by object.

subject: Physics
title: Compound Microscope
description: Total magnification.
derivation:
Product of objective magnification ($m_o$) and eyepiece magnification ($m_e$).
Objective forms real image: $m_o \approx L/f_o$.
Eyepiece acts as simple microscope: $m_e = 1 + D/f_e$.
$MP = m_o \times m_e$.

related_concepts.name: Tube Length
related_concepts.definition: Distance between the second focal point of objective and first focal point of eyepiece.

subject: Physics
title: Telescope
description: Magnifying power (Normal Adjustment).
derivation:
Angle subtended by object $\alpha \approx h/f_o$.
Angle subtended by image $\beta \approx h/f_e$.
$MP = \beta / \alpha = \frac{h/f_e}{h/f_o} = \frac{f_o}{f_e}$.
For high mag, we need large focal length objective.

related_concepts.name: Resolving Power
related_concepts.definition: Ability to distinguish two close objects ($RP = a / 1.22 \lambda$).

subject: Physics
title: Telescope (Near Point)
description: Image formed at near point D.
derivation:
Objective forms image at focus $f_o$.
Eyepiece acts as simple microscope forming image at $D$.
Magnification of eyepiece $m_e = 1 + D/f_e$ is NOT used here directly.
Using Angular Magnification definition $\beta/\alpha$:
$\beta$ is angle subtended by image at $D$.
Result: $MP = \frac{f_o}{f_e} (1 + \frac{f_e}{D})$.

related_concepts.name: Strain on Eye
related_concepts.definition: Maximum magnification causes maximum eye strain (ciliary muscles compressed).

subject: Physics
title: Focal Length (u-v)
description: From Lens Formula.
derivation:
Lens Formula: $1/v - 1/u = 1/f$.
Using sign convention (real object, real image): $u$ is negative, $v$ is positive.
$1/v - 1/(-u) = 1/f \implies 1/v + 1/u = 1/f$.
$\frac{u+v}{uv} = \frac{1}{f}$.
$f = \frac{uv}{u+v}$.

related_concepts.name: Conjugate Foci
related_concepts.definition: Interchangeability of object and image positions for a fixed lens.

subject: Physics
title: Focal Length (u-v Method)
description: Using convex lens. Graph of u vs v is a rectangular hyperbola.
derivation:
From Lens Formula: $\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$.
Using sign convention for real object and real image: $u$ is negative, $v$ is positive.
$\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{-u} = \frac{1}{f} \implies \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$.
$\frac{u+v}{uv} = \frac{1}{f}$.
$f = \frac{uv}{u+v}$.

related_concepts.name: Conjugate Foci
related_concepts.definition: Positions of object and image are interchangeable for a fixed lens.

subject: Physics
title: Combination of Lenses
description: Equivalent focal length for lenses in contact.
derivation:
Lens 1 forms image at $v_1$: $1/v_1 - 1/u = 1/f_1$.
Lens 2 uses $v_1$ as object, forms image at $v$: $1/v - 1/v_1 = 1/f_2$.
Add equations:
$1/v - 1/u = 1/f_1 + 1/f_2$.
Since $1/v - 1/u = 1/F$, $P_{eq} = P_1 + P_2$.

related_concepts.name: Power of Lens
related_concepts.definition: Reciprocal of focal length in meters ($P = 1/f$). Unit: Diopter (D).

subject: Physics
title: Dispersive Power
description: Ability of prism to spread colors.
derivation:
Angular dispersion $\theta = \delta_v - \delta_r$.
Using thin prism approx $\delta = (\mu-1)A$:
$\theta = (\mu_v - 1)A - (\mu_r - 1)A = (\mu_v - \mu_r)A$.
Mean deviation $\delta_y = (\mu_y - 1)A$.
$\omega = \frac{\text{Dispersion}}{\text{Mean Deviation}} = \frac{(\mu_v - \mu_r)A}{(\mu_y - 1)A}$.

related_concepts.name: Achromatic Doublet
related_concepts.definition: Combination of two prisms/lenses to eliminate chromatic aberration (net dispersion = 0).

subject: Physics
title: Thin Prism Deviation
description: Deviation for small prism angle $A$ (typically $< 10^\circ$).
derivation:
General prism formula: $i_1 + i_2 = A + \delta$ and $r_1 + r_2 = A$.
For small angles (paraxial), Snell's law becomes $i \approx \mu r$.
$i_1 = \mu r_1$ and $i_2 = \mu r_2$.
$\delta = (i_1 + i_2) - A = \mu(r_1 + r_2) - A = \mu A - A$.
$\delta = A(\mu - 1)$.

related_concepts.name: Grazing Incidence
related_concepts.definition: Light entering the prism face at $90^\circ$ to the normal.

subject: Physics
title: Resolving Power (Microscope)
description: Inverse of limit of resolution ($d_{min}$).
derivation:
From Airy's diffraction theory, the minimum separation resolvable is:
$d_{min} = \frac{1.22 \lambda}{2\mu \sin \theta}$ (approx $\frac{\lambda}{2\mu \sin \theta}$).
Resolving Power $RP = 1/d_{min}$.
$\mu \sin \theta$ is the Numerical Aperture (NA).

related_concepts.name: Oil Immersion
related_concepts.definition: Using oil ($\\mu > 1$) between objective and sample increases RP.

subject: Physics
title: Resolving Power (Telescope)
description: Ability to separate distant stars.
derivation:
Angular limit of resolution $\Delta \theta$ is the angle of the first diffraction minimum.
$\Delta \theta = \frac{1.22 \lambda}{D}$ ($D$ is aperture).
Resolving Power is the inverse:
$RP = \frac{1}{\Delta \theta} = \frac{D}{1.22 \lambda}$.

related_concepts.name: Large Aperture
related_concepts.definition: Telescopes have large objectives ($D$) to maximize Resolving Power and Light Gathering.

subject: Physics
title: Lateral Shift
description: Perpendicular distance between incident and emergent ray in a glass slab.
derivation:
From geometry of refraction through slab of thickness $t$.
In $\Delta ABC$ (inside slab), hypotenuse $AC = t/\cos r$.
In right $\Delta ACD$ (shift triangle), side $d = AC \sin(i-r)$.
Substitute $AC$: $d = \frac{t}{\cos r} \sin(i-r)$.

related_concepts.name: Normal Shift
related_concepts.definition: Apparent shift in position of object viewed normally: $\Delta x = t(1 - 1/\mu)$.

subject: Physics
title: Silvered Lens Power
description: Equivalent power of a lens with one side silvered (behaves as a mirror).
derivation:
Light passes through the lens ($P_L$), reflects off the mirror ($P_M$), and passes through the lens again ($P_L$).
Total Power $P_{eq} = P_L + P_M + P_L = 2P_L + P_M$.
Note: For a mirror, $P_M = -1/f_m$. For a lens, $P_L = 1/f_l$.
Equivalent Focal Length $F_{eq} = -1/P_{eq}$.

related_concepts.name: Equivalent Mirror
related_concepts.definition: The combination always behaves like a mirror.

subject: Physics
title: Normal Shift
description: Apparent upward shift of an object placed in a denser medium.
derivation:
Real depth = $t$.
Apparent depth $d' = t/\mu$ (for viewing from air).
Shift = Real depth - Apparent depth.
$\Delta t = t - t/\mu = t(1 - 1/\mu)$.

related_concepts.name: Lateral Shift
related_concepts.definition: Sideways shift of light passing through a slab at an angle.

subject: Physics
title: Magnification (Mirror)
description: Linear magnification by a spherical mirror; sign gives orientation. \(m\)=magnification, \(h_i\)=image height, \(h_o\)=object height, \(v\)=image distance, \(u\)=object distance. \(m<0\) inverted/real, \(m>0\) erect/virtual.

subject: Physics
title: Areal Magnification (Mirror)
description: Magnification of a small 2-D area placed perpendicular to axis. \(m_s\)=areal (superficial) magnification, \(m\)=linear magnification, \(v\)=image distance, \(u\)=object distance.

subject: Physics
title: Longitudinal Magnification
description: Magnification of a small object along the principal axis. \(m_L\)=longitudinal magnification, \(m\)=transverse magnification, \(v\)=image distance, \(u\)=object distance. Image is reversed front-to-back.
derivation:
Differentiate mirror formula \(\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}\)
\(-\frac{dv}{v^2}-\frac{du}{u^2}=0\)
\(\frac{dv}{du}=-\frac{v^2}{u^2}=-m^2\)

subject: Physics
title: Power of a Lens
description: Converging power of a lens; SI unit dioptre (D). \(P\)=power in dioptre, \(f\)=focal length in metres (\(+\) for convex, \(-\) for concave). Using cm, divide by 100.

subject: Physics
title: Focal Length & Radius (Mirror)
description: Focal length of a spherical mirror in terms of curvature. \(f\)=focal length, \(R\)=radius of curvature. Valid for paraxial rays.

subject: Physics
title: Power of Combination
description: Net power of two thin lenses separated by distance \(d\). \(P\)=equivalent power, \(P_1,P_2\)=individual powers, \(d\)=separation in metres. For \(d=0\) reduces to \(P=P_1+P_2\).

subject: Physics
title: Refraction at Spherical Surface
description: Single refracting spherical surface relation (Cartesian sign convention). \(\mu_1\)=medium of incidence, \(\mu_2\)=medium of refraction, \(u\)=object distance, \(v\)=image distance, \(R\)=radius of curvature.

subject: Physics
title: Magnification (Spherical Surface)
description: Transverse magnification at a single refracting spherical surface. \(m\)=magnification, \(\mu_1\)=object-side index, \(\mu_2\)=image-side index, \(v\)=image distance, \(u\)=object distance.

subject: Physics
title: Focal Length in a Medium
description: Change of lens focal length when immersed in a medium. \(f_m\)=focal length in medium, \(f_a\)=focal length in air, \(\mu_g\)=lens index, \(\mu_m\)=medium index. If \(\mu_m>\mu_g\) lens nature reverses.

subject: Physics
title: Critical Angle
description: Angle of incidence (denser to rarer) beyond which total internal reflection occurs. \(\theta_c\)=critical angle, \(\mu_1\)=denser medium index, \(\mu_2\)=rarer medium index, \(\mu=\mu_1/\mu_2\). For glass-air \(\mu=1/\sin\theta_c\).

subject: Physics
title: Refractive Index (Real/Apparent Depth)
description: Apparent shallowing of an object viewed normally through a denser medium. \(\mu\)=refractive index of denser medium, \(d\)=real depth, \(d'\)=apparent depth (object appears raised).

subject: Physics
title: Refractive Index & Speed
description: Absolute refractive index from light speed and Snell's law. \(\mu\)=refractive index, \(c\)=speed of light in vacuum, \(v\)=speed in medium, \(i\)=angle of incidence, \(r\)=angle of refraction.

subject: Physics
title: Relative Refractive Index
description: Refractive index of medium 2 w.r.t. medium 1. \({}^1\mu_2\)=relative index, \(\mu\)=absolute indices, \(v\)=wave speeds, \(\lambda\)=wavelengths. Frequency stays constant on refraction.

subject: Physics
title: Prism: i, e, A, \delta Relations
visual_data: A = r_1 + r_2 \quad\therefore\quad \delta = i + e - A
description: Geometry of refraction through a prism. \(A\)=prism angle, \(r_1,r_2\)=refraction angles at the two faces, \(i\)=incidence, \(e\)=emergence, \(\delta\)=deviation. At minimum deviation \(i=e\), \(r_1=r_2\).

subject: Physics
title: Minimum Deviation Condition
description: At minimum deviation a prism passes light symmetrically. \(\delta_m\)=minimum deviation, \(i\)=incidence (=emergence), \(A\)=prism angle, \(r\)=refraction angle at each face.

subject: Physics
title: Maximum Deviation (Prism)
description: Largest deviation when light grazes the first face. \(\delta_{max}\)=maximum deviation, \(e\)=corresponding emergence angle, \(A\)=prism angle, \(i=90^\circ\) (grazing incidence).

subject: Physics
title: Condition for No Emergence (TIR)
description: If prism angle exceeds twice the critical angle, no ray emerges (TIR at second face). \(A\)=prism angle, \(\theta_c\)=critical angle of prism material. Grazing limit gives max \(A=2\theta_c\).

subject: Physics
title: Angular Dispersion
description: Angular spread between violet and red after a thin prism. \(\theta\)=angular dispersion, \(\delta_v,\delta_r\)=deviations of violet/red, \(\mu_v,\mu_r\)=their indices, \(A\)=prism angle.

subject: Physics
title: Newton's Formula (Lens)
description: Object/image distances measured from respective focal points. \(x_1\)=object distance from first focus, \(x_2\)=image distance from second focus, \(f\)=focal length.

subject: Physics
title: Displacement Method (Lens)
description: Focal length from two lens positions giving sharp image on a fixed screen. \(f\)=focal length, \(D\)=object-screen distance, \(d\)=separation between the two lens positions. Needs \(D>4f\).

subject: Physics
title: Object Size (Displacement Method)
description: Object height as geometric mean of the two image sizes in displacement method. \(h_o\)=object size, \(h_1,h_2\)=image sizes at the two lens positions. Also \(m_1 m_2 = 1\).

subject: Physics
title: Astronomical Telescope Length
description: Tube length of a refracting telescope in normal adjustment. \(L\)=length, \(f_o\)=objective focal length, \(f_e\)=eyepiece focal length. Final image at infinity.

subject: Physics
title: Galilean Telescope MP
description: Terrestrial (Galilean) telescope with concave eyepiece gives an erect image. \(MP\)=magnifying power, \(f_o\)=objective focal length, \(f_e\)=eyepiece focal length, \(L\)=tube length.

subject: Physics
title: Cauchy's Dispersion Formula
description: Wavelength dependence of refractive index (normal dispersion). \(\mu\)=refractive index, \(\lambda\)=wavelength, \(A,B\)=Cauchy constants. \(\mu\) larger for violet (shorter \(\lambda\)).

subject: Physics
title: Mirror Velocity Relation (Axial)
description: Axial velocity of image vs object along principal axis of a mirror. \(v_{IM}\)=image velocity (rel. mirror), \(v_{OM}\)=object velocity (rel. mirror), \(m=-v/u\)=magnification.

subject: Physics
title: Sun's Apparent Diameter (Lens)
description: Image size of a distant object subtending small angle at a converging lens/mirror. \(d\)=image diameter, \(f\)=focal length, \(\theta\)=angular size of object in radians.

subject: Physics
title: Two Mirrors: Number of Images
description: Images formed by two plane mirrors inclined at angle \(\theta\) (when \(360/\theta\) is even). \(n\)=number of images, \(\theta\)=angle between mirrors. If \(360/\theta\) odd, count depends on object placement.

subject: Physics
title: Plane Mirror Rotation
description: Reflected ray turns twice the angle the mirror is rotated (fixed incident ray). \(\Delta\)=rotation of reflected ray, \(\theta\)=rotation of mirror. Basis of optical lever.

subject: Physics
title: Lateral Magnification (Two Surfaces)
description: Net magnification through a lens/system equals product of surface (or component) magnifications. \(m\)=net magnification, \(m_1,m_2\)=magnifications of successive refractions/components.

subject: Physics
title: Biot-Savart Law
description: Magnetic field due to current element.
derivation:
An experimental inverse-square law for magnetism.
Field \(dB\) is proportional to current \(I\), element length \(dl\), sine of angle, and \(1/r^2\).
\(dB \propto \frac{I dl \sin \theta}{r^2}\)
Constant of proportionality is \(\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\).

related_concepts.name: Permeability of Free Space
related_concepts.definition: \(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} T\cdot m/A\). Measure of vacuum's support for magnetic fields.

subject: Physics
title: Field: Infinite Wire
description: Field at distance \(r\) from long straight wire.
derivation:
Using Ampere's Circuital Law:
Consider a circular loop of radius \(r\) around the wire.
By symmetry, \(B\) is constant and tangential.
\(\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = B(2\pi r)\)
Current enclosed is \(I\).
\(B(2\pi r) = \mu_0 I\)
\(B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\)

related_concepts.name: Ampere's Law
related_concepts.definition: The line integral of B-field around a closed loop equals \(\mu_0\) times enclosed current.

subject: Physics
title: Field: Arc Center
description: Field at center of circular arc.
derivation:
Use Biot-Savart Law for element \(dl\).
Angle between \(dl\) and \(r\) is always 90° (\(\sin 90 = 1\)).
\(dB = \frac{\mu_0 I dl}{4\pi R^2}\)
Integrate \(dl\) over the arc length \(L = R\theta\):
\(B = \int \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R^2} dl = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R^2} (R\theta)\)
\(B = \frac{\mu_0 I \theta}{4\pi R}\)

related_concepts.name: Right Hand Thumb Rule
related_concepts.definition: Determines direction of magnetic field lines around a current-carrying conductor.

subject: Physics
title: Field: Solenoid
description: Uniform field inside long solenoid.
derivation:
Use Ampere's Law on a rectangular loop partially inside the solenoid.
Only the side inside (length \(h\)) contributes to integral (\(B\cdot h\)).
Sides perpendicular give 0; side outside gives 0 (weak field).
\(\oint B \cdot dl = Bh\)
Enclosed current \(I_{in} = (nh)I\) where \(n\) is turns/length.
\(Bh = \mu_0 (nh I)\)
\(B = \mu_0 n I\)

related_concepts.name: Ideal Solenoid
related_concepts.definition: A solenoid with infinite length, creating a perfectly uniform internal field.

subject: Physics
title: Lorentz Force
description: Magnetic force on moving charge.
derivation:
This is an empirical definition of the Magnetic Field \(B\).
The force is observed to be proportional to charge, velocity, and field, and perpendicular to both \(v\) and \(B\).
Since force is perpendicular to motion, magnetic force does NO WORK.

related_concepts.name: Cyclotron Motion
related_concepts.definition: Circular motion of a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field.

subject: Physics
title: Cyclotron Radius
description: Motion of charge \(q\) entering \(B\) perpendicularly.
derivation:
For circular motion, magnetic force provides centripetal force.
\(F_B = F_c\)
\(qvB = \frac{mv^2}{r}\) (assuming \(v \perp B\))
Cancel \(v\) and solve for \(r\):
\(r = \frac{mv}{qB}\)

related_concepts.name: Time Period
related_concepts.definition: \(T = 2\pi m / qB\). Notably independent of velocity (basis of cyclotron).

subject: Physics
title: Force on Wire
description: Force on straight wire in uniform field.
derivation:
Consider free electrons in wire with drift velocity \(v_d\).
Force on one electron: \(\vec{f} = -e(\vec{v}_d \times \vec{B})\)
Total force = (Force per e) × (Number of e).
\(N = nAl\).
\(\vec{F} = nAl \cdot (-e \vec{v}_d \times \vec{B})\)
Since \(I = -neAv_d\), we substitute \(I\vec{l}\) for \(-neA\vec{v}_d l\):
\(\vec{F} = I(\vec{l} \times \vec{B})\)

related_concepts.name: Fleming's Left Hand Rule
related_concepts.definition: Mnemonic for direction of Force (Thumb), Field (Index), and Current (Middle).

subject: Physics
title: Force: Parallel Wires
description: Force per unit length between currents.
derivation:
Wire 1 creates field \(B_1\) at location of Wire 2.
\(B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 I_1}{2\pi d}\)
Force on length \(l\) of Wire 2: \(F_2 = I_2 l B_1\).
\(F_2 = I_2 l (\frac{\mu_0 I_1}{2\pi d})\)
Force per unit length:
\(\frac{F}{l} = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}\)

related_concepts.name: Definition of Ampere
related_concepts.definition: The current which, in two parallel wires 1m apart, yields force \(2 \times 10^{-7} N/m\).

subject: Physics
title: Magnetic Dipole Moment
description: For a current loop. \(N\): turns, \(A\): area.
derivation:
Defined by analogy to electric dipoles.
A current loop creates a field similar to a bar magnet.
The strength is proportional to current \(I\) and Area \(A\).
Direction is given by Right Hand Curl Rule.

related_concepts.name: Bohr Magneton
related_concepts.definition: The natural unit for expressing the magnetic moment of an electron caused by its orbital or spin angular momentum.

subject: Physics
title: Torque on Dipole
description: Torque aligning dipole with field.
derivation:
Consider a rectangular loop \(a \times b\) in field \(B\).
Forces on sides \(b\) (parallel to axis) cancel.
Forces on sides \(a\) are \(F = IaB\), creating a couple.
Torque \(\tau = F \times (b \sin \theta) = (IaB) (b \sin \theta)\)
\(\tau = I(ab) B \sin \theta = IAB \sin \theta\)
Using \(M = IA\):
\(\vec{\tau} = \vec{M} \times \vec{B}\)

related_concepts.name: Galvanometer Principle
related_concepts.definition: Current-carrying coil in magnetic field experiences torque, deflecting a needle.

subject: Physics
title: Cyclotron Frequency
description: Frequency of charged particle in B-field.
derivation:
Magnetic force provides centripetal force: $qvB = \frac{mv^2}{r}$.
Velocity $v = \frac{qBr}{m}$.
Time period $T = \frac{2\pi r}{v} = \frac{2\pi r}{qBr/m} = \frac{2\pi m}{qB}$.
Frequency $f = 1/T = \frac{qB}{2\pi m}$.
Notice $f$ is independent of $v$ and $r$.

related_concepts.name: Cyclotron
related_concepts.definition: Particle accelerator utilizing the constant frequency of rotation.

subject: Physics
title: Magnetic Pressure
description: Force per unit area.
derivation:
Energy density in field is $u = B^2 / 2\mu_0$.
Work done by magnetic pressure in expanding volume $\Delta V$ is $W = P \Delta V$.
Decrease in field energy $W = u \Delta V$.
Equating work: $P \Delta V = u \Delta V \implies P = u$.
Thus $P_m = B^2 / 2\mu_0$.

related_concepts.name: Solenoid Expansion
related_concepts.definition: Ideally, magnetic pressure tends to expand a current carrying loop or solenoid.

subject: Physics
title: Field on Axis of Coil
description: Magnetic field at distance $x$ from center of current loop.
derivation:
Use Biot-Savart Law. Current element $dl$ is perpendicular to position vector $r$.
$dB = \frac{\mu_0 I dl}{4\pi r^2}$.
Axial component is $dB \sin \alpha = dB (R/r)$.
Integrate over loop ($ \int dl = 2\pi R $).
$B = \int \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r^2} \frac{R}{r} dl = \frac{\mu_0 I R}{4\pi r^3} (2\pi R) = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2r^3}$.
Substitute $r = \sqrt{R^2+x^2}$.

related_concepts.name: Helmholtz Coils
related_concepts.definition: Two identical coils separated by distance $R$ produce a uniform field region.

subject: Physics
title: Ampere's Circuital Law
description: Line integral of field around a closed loop equals current enclosed; used for symmetric field problems. \(B\)=magnetic field, \(d\vec{l}\)=loop element, \(\mu_0\)=permeability of free space, \(I_{enc}\)=net current enclosed by the loop.

subject: Physics
title: Field: Finite Wire
description: Field at perpendicular distance from a finite straight wire. \(r\)=perpendicular distance from wire, \(\theta_1,\theta_2\)=angles subtended by the two ends at the foot of perpendicular, \(I\)=current.

subject: Physics
title: Field: Solenoid End
description: Axial field at the end (mouth) of a long solenoid — half the interior value. \(n\)=turns per unit length, \(I\)=current, \(\mu_0\)=permeability of free space.

subject: Physics
title: Cyclotron Time Period
description: Period of circular motion of a charge in a uniform magnetic field — independent of speed and radius. \(m\)=mass, \(q\)=charge, \(B\)=magnetic field.

subject: Physics
title: Helical Pitch
description: Axial distance advanced per revolution when velocity makes angle with field. \(v\)=speed, \(\theta\)=angle between \(\vec{v}\) and \(\vec{B}\), \(m\)=mass, \(q\)=charge, \(B\)=field.

subject: Physics
title: Cyclotron Max KE
description: Maximum kinetic energy of a particle leaving a cyclotron of dee radius. \(q\)=charge, \(B\)=field, \(R\)=maximum (dee) radius, \(m\)=mass.

subject: Physics
title: Velocity Selector
description: Selected speed when electric and magnetic forces balance (crossed fields). \(E\)=electric field, \(B\)=magnetic field; particle passes undeflected for this \(v\).
derivation:
For no deflection electric and magnetic forces cancel.
\(qE = qvB\)
\(v = \frac{E}{B}\).

subject: Physics
title: Radius vs KE / Momentum
description: Radius of charged particle in field expressed via momentum or kinetic energy. \(p\)=momentum, \(K\)=kinetic energy, \(m\)=mass, \(q\)=charge, \(B\)=field.

subject: Physics
title: Radius via Accelerating PD
description: Radius for a charge accelerated through potential difference then entering field. \(V\)=accelerating potential difference, \(m\)=mass, \(q\)=charge, \(B\)=field.

subject: Physics
title: Lorentz Force (full)
description: Total force on a moving charge in combined electric and magnetic fields. \(q\)=charge, \(\vec{E}\)=electric field, \(\vec{v}\)=velocity, \(\vec{B}\)=magnetic field.

subject: Physics
title: PE of Dipole in Field
description: Orientation potential energy of a magnetic dipole in uniform field (min at \(\theta=0\)). \(M\)=dipole moment, \(B\)=field, \(\theta\)=angle between \(\vec{M}\) and \(\vec{B}\).

subject: Physics
title: Field on Coil Axis (dipole)
description: Far-axial field of a current loop treated as a magnetic dipole (\(x \gg R\)). \(M = NIA\)=dipole moment, \(x\)=distance along axis, \(\mu_0\)=permeability.

subject: Physics
title: Moving Coil Galvanometer
description: Steady deflection of a galvanometer coil proportional to current. \(N\)=turns, \(I\)=current, \(A\)=coil area, \(B\)=field, \(k\)=torsional (restoring) constant of spring.
derivation:
At equilibrium deflecting torque = restoring torque.
\(NIAB = k\phi\)
\(\phi = \frac{NIAB}{k}\).

subject: Physics
title: Galvanometer Sensitivity
description: Current and voltage sensitivities of a moving coil galvanometer. \(S_I\)=current sensitivity, \(S_V\)=voltage sensitivity, \(R\)=coil resistance, \(k\)=spring constant.

subject: Physics
title: Ammeter Shunt
description: Shunt resistance in parallel to convert a galvanometer into an ammeter of range \(I\). \(I_g\)=full-scale galvanometer current, \(G\)=galvanometer resistance, \(I\)=desired max current, \(S\)=shunt.

subject: Physics
title: Voltmeter Series Resistance
description: Series (high) resistance to convert a galvanometer into a voltmeter of range \(V\). \(V\)=desired max voltage, \(I_g\)=full-scale current, \(G\)=galvanometer resistance.

subject: Physics
title: Force on Wire (magnitude)
description: Magnitude of force on a straight current-carrying wire in a uniform field. \(B\)=field, \(I\)=current, \(l\)=length, \(\theta\)=angle between wire and \(\vec{B}\).

subject: Physics
title: Magnetic Moment of e- Orbit
description: Magnetic moment of an electron in a circular orbit and its link to angular momentum. \(e\)=charge, \(v\)=orbital speed, \(r\)=orbit radius, \(L\)=angular momentum, \(m\)=electron mass.

subject: Physics
title: Charge to Moment Ratio
description: Gyromagnetic ratio: ratio of magnetic moment to angular momentum for an orbiting charge. \(M\)=magnetic moment, \(L\)=angular momentum, \(q\)=charge, \(m\)=mass.

subject: Physics
title: Faraday's Law
description: Induced EMF equals negative rate of change of magnetic flux.
derivation:
Experimental law discovered by Michael Faraday.
The magnitude of induced EMF is proportional to rate of change of magnetic flux.
\(|\varepsilon| = \frac{d\Phi}{dt}\)
The negative sign (Lenz's Law) indicates the direction opposes the change.

related_concepts.name: Lenz's Law
related_concepts.definition: The direction of induced current is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it.

subject: Physics
title: Magnetic Flux
description: Scalar product of Magnetic field and Area vector.
derivation:
Flux measures the 'flow' of field lines through a surface.
Defined as dot product \(BA \cos \theta\).
Max flux when surface is perpendicular to field (\(\theta=0\)).
Zero flux when parallel.

related_concepts.name: Weber (Wb)
related_concepts.definition: SI unit of magnetic flux (\(1 Wb = 1 T m^2\)).

subject: Physics
title: Motional EMF
description: EMF induced in a conductor moving in B-field.
derivation:
Conductor of length \(l\) moves with \(v\) in field \(B\).
Force on free electron \(F_m = qvB\) pushes it to one end.
Charge separation creates electric field \(E\) and force \(F_e = qE\).
Equilibrium: \(qE = qvB \Rightarrow E = vB\).
Potential difference (EMF) \(\varepsilon = El = vBl\).

related_concepts.name: Energy Conservation
related_concepts.definition: Mechanical power required to pull the conductor appears as electrical power (\(P = Fv = \varepsilon I\)).

subject: Physics
title: Self Inductance (Solenoid)
description: Inductance of a long solenoid.
derivation:
Total flux linkage \(N\Phi\).
Flux per turn \(\Phi = BA = (\mu_0 n I)A\).
Total turns \(N = nl\).
Total flux \(N\Phi = (nl)(\mu_0 n I A) = \mu_0 n^2 A l I\).
By definition \(N\Phi = LI\).
\(L = \mu_0 n^2 A l\)

related_concepts.name: Back EMF
related_concepts.definition: EMF induced in the inductor opposing the change in current (\(\varepsilon = -L di/dt\)).

subject: Physics
title: Energy in Inductor
description: Magnetic potential energy stored in an inductor.
derivation:
Power required to drive current against back EMF is \(P = |\varepsilon| I = L \frac{di}{dt} I\).
Work done in time \(dt\): \(dW = P dt = L I di\).
Integrate from 0 to \(I\):
\(W = \int_0^I L I di = L [\frac{I^2}{2}]_0^I\)
\(U = \frac{1}{2} L I^2\)

related_concepts.name: Magnetic Energy Density
related_concepts.definition: Energy per unit volume in magnetic field \(u_B = B^2 / 2\mu_0\).

subject: Physics
title: LR Circuit (Growth)
description: Rise of current in an Inductor-Resistor circuit.
derivation:
Apply KVL: $\varepsilon - L \frac{dI}{dt} - IR = 0$.
Rearrange: $\frac{dI}{\varepsilon - IR} = \frac{dt}{L}$.
Integrate ($0$ to $I$, $0$ to $t$):
$-\frac{1}{R} \ln(\varepsilon - IR) = \frac{t}{L}$.
Solving gives $I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R} (1 - e^{-Rt/L})$.

related_concepts.name: Inductive Time Constant
related_concepts.definition: $\tau_L = L/R$. Time for current to reach 63.2% of max value.

subject: Physics
title: LR Circuit (Decay)
description: Decay of current when source is removed.
derivation:
KVL with source removed: $- L \frac{dI}{dt} - IR = 0$ (Current decreases).
$\frac{dI}{I} = -\frac{R}{L} dt$.
Integrate ($I_0$ to $I$, $0$ to $t$):
$\ln(I/I_0) = -\frac{Rt}{L}$.
$I = I_0 e^{-t R/L}$.

related_concepts.name: Magnetic Energy
related_concepts.definition: Energy stored in the inductor ($1/2 LI^2$) is dissipated as heat in the resistor.

subject: Physics
title: Mutual Inductance (Solenoid)
description: Two long coaxial solenoids.
derivation:
Magnetic field due to outer solenoid $B_1 = \mu_0 n_1 I_1$.
Flux through one turn of inner solenoid $\phi_2 = B_1 A$.
Total flux linkage $N_2 \phi_2 = (n_2 l) (\mu_0 n_1 I_1 A)$.
$N_2 \phi_2 = (\mu_0 n_1 n_2 A l) I_1$.
Compare with definition $N_2 \phi_2 = M I_1$.

related_concepts.name: Reciprocity Theorem
related_concepts.definition: $M_{12} = M_{21}$. The mutual inductance is the same regardless of which coil carries current.

subject: Physics
title: Motional EMF (Rotating Rod)
description: EMF across a rod rotating about one end in a perpendicular B-field. \(B\)=field, \(\omega\)=angular speed, \(l\)=rod length (rotation radius).
derivation:
An element at distance \(r\) moves with speed \(v=\omega r\).
\(d\varepsilon = B v\, dr = B\omega r\, dr\).
Integrate: \(\varepsilon = \int_0^l B\omega r\, dr = \frac{1}{2}B\omega l^2\).

related_concepts.name: In terms of frequency
related_concepts.definition: Since \(\omega = 2\pi f\), \(\varepsilon = \pi B f l^2\).

subject: Physics
title: AC Generator EMF
description: EMF of a coil rotating in a uniform field (AC generator). \(N\)=turns, \(B\)=field, \(A\)=coil area, \(\omega\)=angular speed, \(t\)=time.
derivation:
Flux \(\Phi = NBA\cos(\omega t)\).
\(\varepsilon = -\frac{d\Phi}{dt} = NBA\omega\sin(\omega t)\).
Peak EMF \(\varepsilon_0 = NBA\omega\).

related_concepts.name: Peak EMF
related_concepts.definition: Maximum value \(\varepsilon_0 = NBA\omega\), occurring when coil plane is parallel to B.

subject: Physics
title: Self-Inductance Definition
description: Defining relation for self-inductance and the back-EMF it produces. \(N\Phi_B\)=flux linkage, \(L\)=self-inductance, \(I\)=current, \(\varepsilon\)=self-induced (back) EMF.

related_concepts.name: Henry (H)
related_concepts.definition: SI unit of inductance; \(1\,H = 1\,Wb/A = 1\,V\cdot s/A\).

subject: Physics
title: Mutual Inductance Definition
description: Flux linked in coil 2 due to current in coil 1 defines M; EMF induced in coil 2. \(\Phi_{21}\)=flux in 2 per turn due to 1, \(M\)=mutual inductance, \(I_1\)=current in coil 1.

related_concepts.name: Reciprocity
related_concepts.definition: Mutual inductance is symmetric: \(M_{12} = M_{21} = M\).

subject: Physics
title: Coefficient of Coupling
description: Relates mutual inductance to self-inductances via coupling factor. \(M\)=mutual inductance, \(k\)=coupling coefficient \((0 \le k \le 1)\), \(L_1, L_2\)=self-inductances.

related_concepts.name: Perfect Coupling
related_concepts.definition: \(k=1\) when all flux of one coil links the other; then \(M = \sqrt{L_1 L_2}\) (max).

subject: Physics
title: Inductors in Series
description: Equivalent inductance of two coupled inductors in series. \(L_{eq}\)=net inductance, \(L_1, L_2\)=individual inductances, \(M\)=mutual inductance (\(+\) aiding, \(-\) opposing fluxes).

related_concepts.name: No coupling
related_concepts.definition: If \(M=0\) (well separated), \(L_{eq} = L_1 + L_2\) like resistors in series.

subject: Physics
title: Inductors in Parallel
description: Equivalent inductance for inductors in parallel (negligible mutual coupling). \(L_{eq}\)=net inductance, \(L_1, L_2\)=individual inductances.

related_concepts.name: Analogy
related_concepts.definition: Inductors combine like resistors: series adds, parallel reciprocal-adds.

subject: Physics
title: Magnetic Energy Density
description: Energy stored per unit volume in a magnetic field. \(u_B\)=energy density, \(B\)=magnetic field, \(\mu_0\)=permeability of free space.
derivation:
For a solenoid, \(U = \frac{1}{2}LI^2\) with \(L=\mu_0 n^2 A l\) and \(B=\mu_0 nI\).
\(U = \frac{1}{2}\mu_0 n^2 A l I^2 = \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0}(Al)\).
Divide by volume \(Al\): \(u_B = \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0}\).

related_concepts.name: Electric Analogue
related_concepts.definition: Compare with electric field energy density \(u_E = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2\).

subject: Physics
title: Time Constant (LR)
description: Time for current in an LR circuit to reach \(1-1/e\) (63%) of its final value during growth. \(\tau\)=time constant, \(L\)=inductance, \(R\)=resistance.

related_concepts.name: Decay
related_concepts.definition: In one \(\tau\), decaying current falls to \(1/e\) (37%) of its initial value.

subject: Physics
title: Force to Pull Rod (Rails)
description: External force needed to move a conducting rod at constant velocity on rails in a B-field. \(B\)=field, \(l\)=rod length, \(v\)=speed, \(R\)=circuit resistance.
derivation:
EMF \(\varepsilon = Bvl\), induced current \(I = Bvl/R\).
Magnetic force on rod \(F = BIl = \frac{B^2 l^2 v}{R}\) (opposing motion).
Applied force balances this at constant \(v\).

related_concepts.name: Dissipated Power
related_concepts.definition: Mechanical power \(P = Fv = \frac{B^2 l^2 v^2}{R}\) equals heat dissipated \(I^2 R\).

subject: Physics
title: Mutual Inductance (Coaxial Coils)
description: Mutual inductance of a small coil (radius r) at the centre of a large coaxial coil (radius R). \(N_1, N_2\)=turns, \(r\)=small coil radius, \(R\)=large coil radius.

related_concepts.name: Method
related_concepts.definition: Field of large coil \(B = \mu_0 N_1 I/2R\) assumed uniform over the small coil's area.

subject: Physics
title: LC Oscillation Frequency
description: Natural angular frequency of charge/current oscillation in an ideal LC circuit. \(\omega\)=angular frequency, \(L\)=inductance, \(C\)=capacitance.
derivation:
Loop: \(L\frac{d^2q}{dt^2} + \frac{q}{C} = 0\).
SHM form \(\frac{d^2q}{dt^2} = -\omega^2 q\) with \(\omega^2 = 1/LC\).
\(\omega = 1/\sqrt{LC}\), and \(f = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}\).

related_concepts.name: Energy Exchange
related_concepts.definition: Energy shuttles between capacitor \(\frac{q^2}{2C}\) and inductor \(\frac{1}{2}LI^2\); total stays constant.

subject: Physics
title: Maximum Current (LC Circuit)
description: Peak current in LC oscillations from energy conservation. \(I_0\)=peak current, \(q_0\)=peak charge, \(\omega\)=angular frequency.
derivation:
Charge \(q = q_0\cos\omega t\).
Current \(I = -dq/dt = q_0\omega\sin\omega t\).
Peak \(I_0 = q_0\omega\); equivalently \(\frac{1}{2}LI_0^2 = \frac{q_0^2}{2C}\).

related_concepts.name: Phase
related_concepts.definition: Current leads/lags charge by \(\pi/2\); maximum current when capacitor is fully discharged.

subject: Physics
title: RMS Current
description: Root Mean Square value for sinusoidal AC.
derivation:
RMS is the DC equivalent for heating power.
Average power \(P = <I^2 R> = R <I_0^2 \sin^2 \omega t>\).
Average of \(\sin^2\) over a cycle is \(1/2\).
\(P = R \frac{I_0^2}{2}\).
Equating to DC power \(I_{rms}^2 R\):
\(I_{rms}^2 = I_0^2 / 2 \Rightarrow I_{rms} = I_0 / \sqrt{2}\)

related_concepts.name: Peak Value
related_concepts.definition: The maximum amplitude \(I_0\) of the alternating current.

subject: Physics
title: Inductive Reactance
description: Opposition to current flow by inductor.
derivation:
In purely inductive circuit, \(V = L di/dt\).
If \(i = I_0 \sin \omega t\), then \(di/dt = I_0 \omega \cos \omega t\).
\(V = L I_0 \omega \cos \omega t = V_0 \sin(\omega t + \pi/2)\).
Comparing amplitudes: \(V_0 = I_0 (\omega L)\).
This acts like resistance: \(X_L = \omega L\).

related_concepts.name: Phase Lead
related_concepts.definition: In an inductor, voltage leads current by 90° (\(\pi/2\)).

subject: Physics
title: Capacitive Reactance
description: Opposition to current flow by capacitor.
derivation:
In purely capacitive circuit, \(q = CV\).
\(i = dq/dt = C dV/dt\).
If \(V = V_0 \sin \omega t\), then \(i = C V_0 \omega \cos \omega t\).
\(i = \frac{V_0}{1/\omega C} \sin(\omega t + \pi/2)\).
Resistance-like term: \(X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C}\).

related_concepts.name: Phase Lag
related_concepts.definition: In a capacitor, voltage lags behind current by 90° (\(\pi/2\)).

subject: Physics
title: Impedance (LCR)
description: Total opposition in RLC circuit.
derivation:
Using Phasor Diagram:
Resistor voltage \(V_R\) is in phase with \(I\).
Inductor \(V_L\) leads by 90°; Capacitor \(V_C\) lags by 90°.
Net reactive voltage is \(V_L - V_C\).
Total voltage \(V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2}\).
Dividing by \(I\):
\(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}\)

related_concepts.name: Phasor Diagram
related_concepts.definition: Graphical representation of AC voltages and currents as rotating vectors.

subject: Physics
title: Resonance Frequency
description: Frequency where impedance is minimum (Z=R).
derivation:
Resonance occurs when current is maximum.
This happens when Impedance \(Z\) is minimum.
\(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}\) is min when \(X_L = X_C\).
\(\omega L = \frac{1}{\omega C}\)
\(\omega^2 = \frac{1}{LC}\)
\(\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\)

related_concepts.name: Q-Factor
related_concepts.definition: Quality factor, determines sharpness of resonance (\(Q = \frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}\)).

subject: Physics
title: Power Factor
description: Ratio of true power to apparent power.
derivation:
Average power in AC: \(P = V_{rms} I_{rms} \cos \phi\).
From impedance triangle:
Base is \(R\), Hypotenuse is \(Z\), Angle is \(\phi\).
\(\cos \phi = \text{Adjacent}/\text{Hypotenuse} = R/Z\).
Max power at resonance (\(\cos \phi = 1\)).

related_concepts.name: Wattless Current
related_concepts.definition: Current component in pure inductor/capacitor that consumes zero average power.

subject: Physics
title: Transformer Ratio
description: Ideal transformer relation.
derivation:
Based on Faraday's Law.
Flux \(\Phi\) is same through primary and secondary (ideal core).
\(V_p = -N_p \frac{d\Phi}{dt}\)
\(V_s = -N_s \frac{d\Phi}{dt}\)
Dividing equations: \(\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}\).
For power conservation (\(P_{in} = P_{out}\)): \(V_p I_p = V_s I_s\).

related_concepts.name: Step-Up/Step-Down
related_concepts.definition: Step-up increases voltage (\(N_s > N_p\)); Step-down decreases voltage.

subject: Physics
title: Quality Factor
description: Sharpness of resonance.
derivation:
Ratio of Voltage across L or C to Applied Voltage at resonance.
$Q = \frac{V_L}{V_R} = \frac{I \omega_0 L}{I R} = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R}$.
Substitute $\omega_0 = 1/\sqrt{LC}$:
$Q = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} \frac{L}{R} = \frac{1}{R} \sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}$.

related_concepts.name: Selectivity
related_concepts.definition: High Q circuits are highly selective, rejecting frequencies other than $\omega_0$.

subject: Physics
title: LC Oscillations
description: Natural frequency of ideal LC circuit.
derivation:
Kirchhoff's Law: $V_L + V_C = 0$.
$L \frac{di}{dt} + \frac{q}{C} = 0$.
Since $i = dq/dt$, $L \frac{d^2q}{dt^2} + \frac{q}{C} = 0$.
$\frac{d^2q}{dt^2} + \frac{1}{LC}q = 0$.
Compare with SHM $\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} + \omega^2 x = 0$.
$\omega^2 = 1/LC$.

related_concepts.name: Energy Exchange
related_concepts.definition: Energy oscillates between Electric (Capacitor) and Magnetic (Inductor) forms.

subject: Physics
title: Average AC (Half Cycle)
description: Mean value of sinusoidal current over a positive half cycle.
derivation:
$I_{avg} = \frac{\int_0^{T/2} I_0 \sin(\omega t) dt}{\int_0^{T/2} dt}$.
Denominator is $T/2$.
Numerator integrates to $\frac{I_0}{\omega} [-\cos(\omega t)]_0^{T/2} = \frac{I_0}{\omega} (1+1) = \frac{2I_0}{\omega}$.
Ratio: $\frac{2I_0/\omega}{\pi/\omega} = \frac{2I_0}{\pi}$.

related_concepts.name: Full Cycle Average
related_concepts.definition: The average value of AC over a complete cycle is zero.

subject: Physics
title: RMS Voltage
description: DC-equivalent (heating) value of sinusoidal AC voltage. \(V_{rms}\)=rms voltage, \(V_0\)=peak voltage.
derivation:
For \(V = V_0 \sin \omega t\), rms is the square root of the mean of \(V^2\).
\(V_{rms}^2 = <V_0^2 \sin^2 \omega t>\)
Mean of \(\sin^2\) over a full cycle \(= 1/2\).
\(V_{rms}^2 = V_0^2/2\)
\(V_{rms} = V_0/\sqrt{2}\)

related_concepts.name: Mains Voltage
related_concepts.definition: The 220 V Indian mains is the rms value; its peak is \(V_0 = 220\sqrt{2} \approx 311\) V.

subject: Physics
title: Average Power in AC
description: True (dissipated) power in an AC circuit. \(V_{rms},I_{rms}\)=rms voltage and current, \(\cos\phi\)=power factor.
derivation:
Let \(V = V_0 \sin \omega t\), \(i = I_0 \sin(\omega t - \phi)\).
Instantaneous power \(P = Vi = V_0 I_0 \sin \omega t \sin(\omega t - \phi)\).
Averaging over a cycle, the cross term vanishes.
\(P_{avg} = \frac{V_0 I_0}{2}\cos\phi = V_{rms} I_{rms}\cos\phi\)

related_concepts.name: Apparent Power
related_concepts.definition: The product \(V_{rms} I_{rms}\) (in VA), without the power-factor term.

related_concepts.name: Resonance Power
related_concepts.definition: At resonance \(\cos\phi = 1\), so power is maximum \(P = V_{rms} I_{rms}\).

subject: Physics
title: Phase Angle (LCR)
description: Phase difference between voltage and current in a series LCR circuit. \(\phi\)=phase angle, \(X_L,X_C\)=reactances, \(R\)=resistance.
derivation:
From the impedance phasor triangle, the net reactance \((X_L - X_C)\) is perpendicular to \(R\).
\(\tan\phi = \frac{\text{net reactance}}{R} = \frac{X_L - X_C}{R}\)
If \(X_L > X_C\): circuit is inductive, current lags.
If \(X_C > X_L\): circuit is capacitive, current leads.

related_concepts.name: Resonance
related_concepts.definition: At \(X_L = X_C\), \(\phi = 0\); voltage and current are in phase.

subject: Physics
title: Instantaneous AC Voltage & Current
visual_data: V = V_0 \sin \omega t, \quad i = I_0 \sin(\omega t \pm \phi)
description: Time-varying forms of sinusoidal AC. \(V_0,I_0\)=peak values, \(\omega\)=angular frequency, \(\phi\)=phase difference.

related_concepts.name: Angular Frequency
related_concepts.definition: \(\omega = 2\pi f\), where \(f\) is the supply frequency (50 Hz for Indian mains).

related_concepts.name: Phase Sign
related_concepts.definition: Current lags (\(-\phi\)) in inductive circuits, leads (\(+\phi\)) in capacitive circuits.

subject: Physics
title: Wattless Current
description: Component of current that dissipates no average power. \(I_{rms}\)=rms current, \(\phi\)=phase angle.
derivation:
Resolve current into two components relative to voltage.
In-phase component \(I_{rms}\cos\phi\) carries the true power.
Quadrature component \(I_{rms}\sin\phi\) is \(90^\circ\) out of phase with \(V\).
Its average power \(= V_{rms}(I_{rms}\sin\phi)\cos 90^\circ = 0\).

related_concepts.name: Pure Reactance
related_concepts.definition: An ideal inductor or capacitor (\(\phi = 90^\circ\)) carries fully wattless current.

subject: Physics
title: Resonant Current (Max)
description: Peak rms current in a series LCR circuit at resonance. \(V_{rms}\)=rms supply voltage, \(R\)=resistance.
derivation:
At resonance \(X_L = X_C\), so impedance \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + 0} = R\) (minimum).
Current \(I_{rms} = V_{rms}/Z\) is therefore maximum.
\(I_{max} = V_{rms}/R\)

related_concepts.name: Acceptor Circuit
related_concepts.definition: A series LCR circuit at resonance, which accepts maximum current at \(\omega_0\).

subject: Physics
title: Bandwidth of Resonance
description: Width of the resonance curve between half-power points. \(\Delta\omega\)=bandwidth, \(R\)=resistance, \(L\)=inductance, \(\omega_0\)=resonant frequency, \(Q\)=quality factor.
derivation:
Half-power points occur where current is \(1/\sqrt{2}\) of maximum.
There \(|X_L - X_C| = R\), giving frequencies \(\omega_1,\omega_2\).
Bandwidth \(\Delta\omega = \omega_2 - \omega_1 = R/L\).
Since \(Q = \omega_0 L/R\), this is \(\omega_0/Q\).

related_concepts.name: Sharpness
related_concepts.definition: Sharpness of resonance \(= \omega_0/\Delta\omega = Q\); larger \(Q\) gives a narrower, sharper peak.

subject: Physics
title: Q-Factor (Bandwidth Form)
description: Sharpness of resonance as the ratio of resonant frequency to bandwidth. \(\omega_0\)=resonant frequency, \(\Delta\omega\)=bandwidth, \(L\)=inductance, \(R\)=resistance.
derivation:
Quality factor measures how sharply current peaks at resonance.
\(Q = \frac{\text{resonant freq}}{\text{bandwidth}} = \frac{\omega_0}{\Delta\omega}\)
With \(\Delta\omega = R/L\):
\(Q = \frac{\omega_0}{R/L} = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R}\)

related_concepts.name: Voltage Magnification
related_concepts.definition: At resonance the voltage across L (or C) is \(Q\) times the supply voltage.

subject: Physics
title: Power in Pure R / L / C
description: Average power dissipated in ideal single-element AC circuits. \(P_R,P_L,P_C\)=average powers in resistor, inductor, capacitor.
derivation:
Average power \(P = V_{rms} I_{rms}\cos\phi\).
Pure resistor: \(\phi = 0 \Rightarrow \cos\phi = 1 \Rightarrow P_R = V_{rms} I_{rms}\).
Pure inductor/capacitor: \(\phi = 90^\circ \Rightarrow \cos\phi = 0\).
\(\therefore P_L = P_C = 0\) (energy only stored and returned).

related_concepts.name: Ideal Reactor
related_concepts.definition: An ideal inductor or capacitor stores and returns energy each cycle with zero net dissipation.

subject: Physics
title: Energy in LC Oscillations
description: Total conserved energy in an ideal (resistanceless) LC circuit. \(q\)=charge on capacitor, \(C\)=capacitance, \(L\)=inductance, \(i\)=current.
derivation:
Energy oscillates between the capacitor (electric) and inductor (magnetic).
Electric energy \(U_E = q^2/2C\); magnetic energy \(U_B = \tfrac12 L i^2\).
With no resistance, no energy is lost: \(U_E + U_B = \text{const}\).
Peak: \(\tfrac12 L I_0^2 = \frac{q_0^2}{2C}\).

related_concepts.name: Charge–Mass Analogy
related_concepts.definition: LC oscillations mirror SHM: \(q \leftrightarrow x\), \(L \leftrightarrow m\), \(1/C \leftrightarrow k\).

subject: Physics
title: Charge in LC Oscillation
description: Time variation of capacitor charge and circuit current in an ideal LC loop. \(q_0\)=max charge, \(\omega = 1/\sqrt{LC}\).
derivation:
Kirchhoff's law: \(L\frac{d^2q}{dt^2} + \frac{q}{C} = 0\).
This is SHM with \(\omega = 1/\sqrt{LC}\).
Solution: \(q = q_0 \cos\omega t\).
Current \(i = dq/dt = -q_0\omega\sin\omega t\), with peak \(I_0 = q_0\omega\).

related_concepts.name: Phase Difference
related_concepts.definition: Charge and current are \(90^\circ\) out of phase in LC oscillations.

subject: Physics
title: Ideal Transformer Relation
description: Voltage, turns and current relations for a 100%-efficient transformer. \(V\)=voltage, \(N\)=turns, \(I\)=current; subscripts \(p\)=primary, \(s\)=secondary.
derivation:
For an ideal transformer, output power = input power.
\(V_p I_p = V_s I_s\)
\(\Rightarrow \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{I_p}{I_s}\)
Combined with the flux-linkage turns ratio \(V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p\).

related_concepts.name: Step-up / Step-down
related_concepts.definition: \(N_s > N_p\) steps voltage up (current down); \(N_s < N_p\) steps it down.

related_concepts.name: Transformer Efficiency
related_concepts.definition: \(\eta = \frac{P_{out}}{P_{in}} = \frac{V_s I_s}{V_p I_p}\); ideal transformer has \(\eta = 1\).

subject: Physics
title: Form Factor
description: Ratio of rms to half-cycle average value for sinusoidal AC. \(I_{rms}\)=rms current, \(I_{avg}\)=average over half cycle.
derivation:
For a sine wave: \(I_{rms} = I_0/\sqrt{2}\) and \(I_{avg} = 2I_0/\pi\).
\(k_f = \frac{I_0/\sqrt{2}}{2I_0/\pi} = \frac{\pi}{2\sqrt{2}} \approx 1.11\)

related_concepts.name: Peak Factor
related_concepts.definition: Ratio of peak to rms value: \(I_0/I_{rms} = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414\) for a sine wave.

subject: Physics
title: Impedance of L-R / C-R
description: Impedance of series RL and RC circuits. \(R\)=resistance, \(X_L=\omega L\), \(X_C=1/\omega C\).
derivation:
Resistance and reactance phasors are perpendicular.
Series RL: \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}\), current lags by \(\tan\phi = X_L/R\).
Series RC: \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_C^2}\), current leads by \(\tan\phi = X_C/R\).

related_concepts.name: Special Case of LCR
related_concepts.definition: Set \(X_C = 0\) (RL) or \(X_L = 0\) (RC) in the general LCR impedance formula.

subject: Physics
title: Voltage Across L & C at Resonance
description: Voltage magnification across reactive elements at series resonance. \(Q\)=quality factor, \(V_{source}\)=supply voltage.
derivation:
At resonance current is \(I = V_{source}/R\).
\(V_L = I X_L = \frac{V_{source}}{R}\omega_0 L = Q V_{source}\) since \(Q = \omega_0 L/R\).
Equal and opposite \(V_C\) cancels \(V_L\), leaving \(V_{source} = V_R\).

related_concepts.name: Voltage Cancellation
related_concepts.definition: \(V_L\) and \(V_C\) are \(180^\circ\) out of phase and cancel; net reactive voltage is zero at resonance.

subject: Physics
title: Phase: Pure R, L, C
description: Phase of current relative to voltage in pure elements. In pure \(R\), \(V\) and \(i\) are in phase (\(\phi=0\)); in pure \(L\), current lags voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\); in pure \(C\), current leads voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).

subject: Physics
title: AC through Resistor
description: Purely resistive AC circuit; current is in phase with voltage. \(V_0\)=peak voltage, \(R\)=resistance, \(I_{rms}\)/\(V_{rms}\)=rms current/voltage, \(\omega\)=angular frequency.

subject: Physics
title: Current in Pure Inductor
description: Current in a purely inductive AC circuit; lags voltage by \(90^{\circ}\). \(X_L=\omega L\)=inductive reactance, \(V_0\)=peak voltage, \(I_0\)=peak current.

subject: Physics
title: Current in Pure Capacitor
description: Current in a purely capacitive AC circuit; leads voltage by \(90^{\circ}\). \(X_C=\frac{1}{\omega C}\)=capacitive reactance, \(V_0\)=peak voltage, \(I_0\)=peak current.

subject: Physics
title: Apparent vs Real Power
description: Apparent power (VA) vs real power (W) in an AC circuit; \(\cos\phi\) is the power factor. \(V_{rms}\), \(I_{rms}\)=rms voltage/current, \(\phi\)=phase angle.

subject: Physics
title: Peak Current (LCR)
description: Peak current in a series LCR circuit driven by an AC source. \(V_0\)=peak voltage, \(Z\)=impedance, \(X_L\), \(X_C\)=inductive/capacitive reactance.

subject: Physics
title: Frequency-Period Relation
description: Links angular frequency, ordinary frequency and time period of an AC source. \(\omega\)=angular frequency, \(f\)=frequency, \(T\)=time period.

subject: Physics
title: Resonance: X_L = X_C
description: At series resonance reactances cancel, impedance is minimum (\(=R\)), current is maximum and circuit is purely resistive. \(X_L\), \(X_C\)=reactances, \(Z\)=impedance.

subject: Physics
title: Resonant Frequency (Hz)
description: Series LCR resonance frequency in hertz. \(L\)=inductance, \(C\)=capacitance, \(f_0\)=resonant frequency.

subject: Physics
title: Transformer Efficiency
description: Ratio of output to input power for a real transformer (<1 due to losses). \(V_s\), \(I_s\)=secondary voltage/current, \(V_p\), \(I_p\)=primary voltage/current.

subject: Physics
title: Drift Velocity
description: Avg velocity of electrons.
derivation:
Force on electron \(F = eE\).
Acceleration \(a = eE/m\).
Electrons accelerate for average time \(\tau\) (relaxation time) before collision.
\(v_d = a \tau = \frac{eE}{m}\tau\).
Relation to current: \(I = nAe v_d\).

related_concepts.name: Relaxation Time
related_concepts.definition: Average time interval between two successive collisions of electrons.

subject: Physics
title: Current Density
description: Vector form of Ohm's Law.
derivation:
Current density \(J = I/A\).
Substitute \(I = nAe v_d\): \(J = ne v_d\).
Substitute \(v_d = \frac{eE\tau}{m}\):
\(J = \frac{ne^2\tau}{m} E\)
The term \(\frac{ne^2\tau}{m}\) is conductivity \(\sigma\).
\(\vec{J} = \sigma \vec{E}\)

related_concepts.name: Conductivity
related_concepts.definition: Measure of a material's ability to conduct current (Inverse of resistivity).

subject: Physics
title: Resistivity (Temp)
description: Linear approx for metals.
derivation:
For metals, resistivity increases with temperature due to increased collisions (lower \(\tau\)).
Approximated as a linear expansion series around reference \(T_0\).
\(\Delta \rho \propto \Delta T\) and original \(\rho_0\).
\(\Delta \rho = \rho_0 \alpha \Delta T\)
\(\rho_T = \rho_0 + \rho_0 \alpha (T-T_0)\)

related_concepts.name: Temp Coefficient
related_concepts.definition: \(\alpha\): Fractional change in resistivity per degree change in temperature.

subject: Physics
title: KCL (Current Law)
description: Conservation of charge at a junction.
derivation:
Based on Conservation of Charge.
Charge cannot accumulate at a junction point (node) in steady state.
Total charge entering per second must equal total charge leaving per second.

related_concepts.name: Nodal Analysis
related_concepts.definition: Circuit analysis method using KCL to find node voltages.

subject: Physics
title: KVL (Voltage Law)
description: Conservation of energy in a closed loop.
derivation:
Based on Conservation of Energy.
Electrostatic force is conservative.
Work done moving a unit charge around a closed loop is zero.
Sum of potential drops (resistors) and gains (batteries) is zero.

related_concepts.name: Mesh Analysis
related_concepts.definition: Circuit analysis method using KVL to find loop currents.

subject: Physics
title: Wheatstone Bridge
description: Null point condition. No current flows through the galvanometer.
derivation:
Bridge is balanced when potential at nodes B and D is equal ($V_B = V_D$).
Current through galvanometer $I_g = 0$.
Apply KVL to left loop: $I_1 R_1 - I_3 R_3 = 0 \implies I_1 R_1 = I_3 R_3$.
Apply KVL to right loop: $I_2 R_2 - I_4 R_4 = 0 \implies I_2 R_2 = I_4 R_4$.
Since $I_g=0$, $I_1 = I_2$ and $I_3 = I_4$.
Dividing equations: $\frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{R_3}{R_4}$

related_concepts.name: Null Method
related_concepts.definition: Measurement technique where zero reading indicates balance, eliminating error due to internal resistance of the meter.

subject: Physics
title: Meter Bridge
description: Unknown resistance $R$ using standard $S$ and balance length $l$.
derivation:
Based on Wheatstone Bridge principle.
Wire AC is 100cm long with uniform resistance per cm $\rho$.
Resistance of length $l$: $P = \rho l$.
Resistance of length $(100-l)$: $Q = \rho(100-l)$.
At balance: $\frac{R}{S} = \frac{P}{Q} = \frac{\rho l}{\rho(100-l)}$.
$R = S \frac{l}{100-l}$

related_concepts.name: End Error
related_concepts.definition: Error caused when the zero mark of the scale does not coincide exactly with the start of the bridge wire.

subject: Physics
title: Potentiometer (EMF)
description: Comparing EMFs of two cells using balancing lengths.
derivation:
Potential drop across potentiometer wire is proportional to length ($V \propto l$).
For cell 1, balance length is $l_1$: $\varepsilon_1 = k l_1$.
For cell 2, balance length is $l_2$: $\varepsilon_2 = k l_2$.
Dividing the two equations eliminates the potential gradient $k$.
$\frac{\varepsilon_1}{\varepsilon_2} = \frac{l_1}{l_2}$

related_concepts.name: Potential Gradient
related_concepts.definition: Potential drop per unit length along the potentiometer wire ($k = V/L$).

subject: Physics
title: Internal Resistance
description: Internal resistance of cell via Potentiometer.
derivation:
Open circuit (no current drawn): $\varepsilon = k l_1$.
Closed circuit with external $R$: Terminal voltage $V = k l_2$.
We know $V = \frac{\varepsilon R}{R+r}$.
$\frac{\varepsilon}{V} = \frac{l_1}{l_2} = \frac{R+r}{R}$.
$\frac{l_1}{l_2} = 1 + \frac{r}{R}$.
$r = R(\frac{l_1}{l_2} - 1)$

related_concepts.name: Terminal Voltage
related_concepts.definition: Voltage output of a source when current is flowing ($V = \varepsilon - Ir$).

subject: Physics
title: Power in Circuit
description: Rate of heat dissipation or energy consumption.
derivation:
Work done moving charge $dQ$ across potential $V$ is $dW = V dQ$.
Power $P = \frac{dW}{dt} = V \frac{dQ}{dt} = VI$.
Using Ohm's Law ($V=IR$):
1. $P = (IR)I = I^2 R$ (Series/Current constant).
2. $P = V(V/R) = V^2/R$ (Parallel/Voltage constant).

related_concepts.name: Joule Heating
related_concepts.definition: Process where energy of electric current is converted into heat ($H = I^2 Rt$).

subject: Physics
title: Max Power Transfer
description: Condition for max power delivery to load.
derivation:
Current $I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R+r}$.
Power $P = I^2 R = \frac{\varepsilon^2 R}{(R+r)^2}$.
To find max, set $dP/dR = 0$.
$\frac{dP}{dR} = \varepsilon^2 \frac{(R+r)^2(1) - R(2)(R+r)}{(R+r)^4} = 0$.
$(R+r) - 2R = 0 \implies r = R$.

related_concepts.name: Efficiency at Max Power
related_concepts.definition: At maximum power transfer, efficiency is only 50% ($\eta = R/(R+r)$).

subject: Physics
title: Color Code (Resistor)
description: BBROYGBVGW (Black 0, Brown 1, Red 2... White 9).
derivation:
Mnemonic: "**B**lack **B**rown **R**ods **O**f **Y**our **G**ate **B**ecome **V**ery **G**ood **W**hen (given Silver/Gold)".
Band 1 (A): 1st digit.
Band 2 (B): 2nd digit.
Band 3 (C): Multiplier ($10^C$).
Band 4 (D): Tolerance (Gold 5%, Silver 10%).

related_concepts.name: Tolerance
related_concepts.definition: The percentage error or precision of the resistor value.

subject: Physics
title: Ohm's Law
description: Relates potential difference across a conductor to current through it. \(V\)=voltage, \(I\)=current, \(R\)=resistance.

subject: Physics
title: Resistance Formula
description: Resistance of a uniform conductor in terms of geometry. \(\rho\)=resistivity, \(l\)=length, \(A\)=cross-sectional area.

subject: Physics
title: Electric Current
description: Rate of flow of charge through a cross-section. \(I\)=current, \(q\)=charge, \(t\)=time.

subject: Physics
title: Current (Microscopic)
description: Current in terms of charge carriers and drift speed. \(n\)=number density of electrons, \(e\)=electron charge, \(A\)=area, \(v_d\)=drift velocity.

subject: Physics
title: Conductivity & Mobility
description: Microscopic conductivity from free-electron model. \(\sigma\)=conductivity, \(n\)=electron density, \(\tau\)=relaxation time, \(m\)=electron mass, \(\mu\)=mobility.

subject: Physics
title: Mobility
description: Drift speed per unit electric field. \(\mu\)=mobility, \(v_d\)=drift velocity, \(E\)=field, \(\tau\)=relaxation time, \(m\)=mass.

subject: Physics
title: Resistivity (Microscopic)
description: Resistivity from relaxation-time model. \(m\)=electron mass, \(n\)=electron density, \(e\)=charge, \(\tau\)=relaxation time.

subject: Physics
title: Resistors in Series
description: Net resistance of resistors joined end to end (same current). \(R_s\)=equivalent resistance.

subject: Physics
title: Resistors in Parallel
description: Net resistance of resistors across same two nodes (same voltage). \(R_p\)=equivalent resistance.

subject: Physics
title: EMF & Terminal Voltage
description: Cell driving current through external resistance with internal resistance. \(\varepsilon\)=emf, \(V\)=terminal voltage, \(I\)=current, \(r\)=internal resistance, \(R\)=external resistance.

subject: Physics
title: Terminal Voltage (Discharging)
description: Terminal p.d. when cell supplies current. \(V\)=terminal voltage, \(\varepsilon\)=emf, \(I\)=current, \(r\)=internal resistance.

subject: Physics
title: Internal Resistance (from V)
description: Internal resistance from emf, terminal voltage and load. \(\varepsilon\)=emf, \(V\)=terminal voltage, \(R\)=external resistance.

subject: Physics
title: Cells in Series
description: n identical cells in series driving load R. \(\varepsilon\)=emf per cell, \(r\)=internal resistance per cell, \(n\)=number of cells, \(R\)=external resistance.

subject: Physics
title: Mixed Grouping (Max Current)
description: n cells per row, m rows in parallel; current is maximum when \(R = nr/m\). \(\varepsilon\)=emf per cell, \(r\)=internal resistance per cell, \(R\)=load.

subject: Physics
title: Joule's Heating Law
visual_data: H = I^2 R t = \frac{V^2}{R} t = VIt
description: Heat dissipated in a resistor over time t. \(H\)=heat (J), \(I\)=current, \(R\)=resistance, \(V\)=voltage, \(t\)=time.

subject: Physics
title: Drift Velocity & Current Density
description: Current density linking macroscopic and microscopic quantities. \(J\)=current density, \(I\)=current, \(A\)=area, \(n\)=electron density, \(v_d\)=drift velocity, \(\sigma\)=conductivity, \(E\)=field.

subject: Physics
title: Conductance & Conductivity
description: Reciprocal quantities of resistance and resistivity. \(G\)=conductance (siemens), \(R\)=resistance, \(\sigma\)=conductivity, \(\rho\)=resistivity.

subject: Physics
title: Temperature Coefficient
description: Fractional change of resistance per degree. \(\alpha\)=temperature coefficient, \(R_T\)=resistance at T, \(R_0\)=resistance at \(T_0\).

subject: Physics
title: Ammeter Shunt
description: Shunt resistance to convert galvanometer into ammeter of range I. \(S\)=shunt, \(I_g\)=full-scale galvanometer current, \(G\)=galvanometer resistance, \(I\)=desired range.

subject: Physics
title: Voltmeter Series Resistance
description: Series resistance to convert galvanometer into voltmeter of range V. \(R\)=series resistance, \(V\)=desired range, \(I_g\)=full-scale current, \(G\)=galvanometer resistance.

subject: Physics
title: Wheatstone Galvanometer Current
description: Balance condition: no current through galvanometer when bridge is balanced. \(P, Q, R, S\)=four arm resistances, \(I_g\)=galvanometer current.

subject: Physics
title: RC Charging (Capacitor)
visual_data: q = q_0 \left( 1 - e^{-t/RC} \right), \quad I = I_0 e^{-t/RC}
description: Charge growth and current decay while charging a capacitor through R. \(q_0\)=final charge, \(I_0=\varepsilon/R\)=initial current, \(RC\)=time constant, \(t\)=time.

subject: Physics
title: RC Discharging & Time Constant
description: Charge decay during discharge; \(\tau\) is time to fall to \(1/e\) of initial. \(q_0\)=initial charge, \(R\)=resistance, \(C\)=capacitance, \(t\)=time.

subject: Physics
title: Wire Stretching (Resistance)
description: How resistance scales when a wire of fixed volume is stretched. \(R\)=resistance, \(l\)=length, \(A\)=cross-section area (volume constant).
derivation:
Volume \(V = Al\) constant \(\Rightarrow A = V/l\)
R = \rho l/A = \rho l^2 / V
\therefore R \propto l^2

subject: Physics
title: Heater / Bulb Resistance
description: Resistance of an appliance from its power rating. \(V\)=rated voltage, \(P\)=rated power, \(R\)=resistance.

subject: Physics
title: Bulbs in Series (Power)
description: Combined power of appliances in series at rated voltage (lower-power one glows brighter). \(P_1, P_2\)=rated powers, \(P_{net}\)=net power.

subject: Physics
title: Bulbs in Parallel (Power)
description: Combined power of appliances in parallel at rated voltage (higher-power one glows brighter). \(P_i\)=rated power of each.

subject: Physics
title: Galvanometer (Ohmic) Voltage
description: Voltage across a galvanometer at deflection. \(V_g\)=voltage, \(I_g\)=galvanometer current, \(G\)=galvanometer resistance.

subject: Physics
title: Current Divider Rule
description: Current through one of two parallel resistors. \(I\)=total current, \(R_1, R_2\)=parallel resistances, \(I_1\)=current in \(R_1\).

subject: Physics
title: Maximum Power Delivered
description: Maximum power transferred to load when \(R = r\). \(\varepsilon\)=emf, \(r\)=internal resistance.

subject: Physics
title: Gravitational Field
description: Field strength at surface of planet mass $M$, radius $R$.
derivation:
Force on mass $m$ at surface: $F = \frac{G M m}{R^2}$.
Acceleration due to gravity $g = \frac{F}{m}$.
$g = \frac{GM}{R^2}$

related_concepts.name: Universal Gravitational Constant
related_concepts.definition: $G \approx 6.67 \times 10^{-11} N m^2/kg^2$.

subject: Physics
title: Variation of g (Height)
description: Valid for small heights $h \ll R$.
derivation:
At height $h$: $g_h = \frac{GM}{(R+h)^2} = \frac{GM}{R^2(1+h/R)^2}$.
$g_h = g (1 + \frac{h}{R})^{-2}$.
Using Binomial expansion for $x \ll 1$: $(1+x)^n \approx 1+nx$.
$g_h \approx g (1 - \frac{2h}{R})$

related_concepts.name: Binomial Approximation
related_concepts.definition: Mathematical tool $(1+x)^n \approx 1+nx$ used when $x$ is very small.

subject: Physics
title: Variation of g (Depth)
description: Acceleration due to gravity at depth $d$.
derivation:
At depth $d$, only the inner sphere of radius $(R-d)$ contributes.
Mass $M' = \frac{M}{4/3\pi R^3} \times \frac{4}{3}\pi (R-d)^3 = M \frac{(R-d)^3}{R^3}$.
$g_d = \frac{G M'}{(R-d)^2} = \frac{G M (R-d)}{R^3}$.
Substitute $g = GM/R^2$: $g_d = g \frac{R-d}{R} = g(1 - d/R)$.

related_concepts.name: Shell Theorem
related_concepts.definition: A spherical shell exerts no gravitational force on a particle inside it.

subject: Physics
title: Escape Velocity
description: Min speed to escape gravitational field.
derivation:
Conservation of Energy: Initial Total Energy = Final Total Energy (at $\infty$).
$K_i + U_i = 0$ (Just escapes).
$\frac{1}{2}m v_e^2 - \frac{GMm}{R} = 0$.
$v_e^2 = \frac{2GM}{R}$.
$v_e = \sqrt{2gR}$

related_concepts.name: Binding Energy
related_concepts.definition: Energy required to move a satellite from its orbit to infinity.

subject: Physics
title: Orbital Velocity
description: Speed of satellite in circular orbit.
derivation:
Gravitational force provides necessary centripetal force.
$F_g = F_c \implies \frac{GMm}{r^2} = \frac{m v_o^2}{r}$.
$v_o^2 = \frac{GM}{r}$.
$v_o = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{r}}$

related_concepts.name: Geostationary Orbit
related_concepts.definition: Orbit where $T=24$ hrs, keeping satellite fixed relative to Earth.

subject: Physics
title: Kepler's Third Law
description: Square of time period proportional to cube of radius.
derivation:
Time period $T = \frac{\text{Circumference}}{\text{Speed}} = \frac{2\pi r}{v_o}$.
Substitute $v_o = \sqrt{GM/r}$.
$T = 2\pi r \sqrt{\frac{r}{GM}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{r^3}{GM}}$.
Squaring both sides:
$T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{GM} r^3$

related_concepts.name: Areal Velocity
related_concepts.definition: Kepler's 2nd Law: Areal velocity ($dA/dt$) is constant ($L/2m$).

subject: Physics
title: Gravitational PE
