description: Potential energy of two masses at separation $r$.
derivation:
Work done by external agent to bring mass $m$ from infinity to $r$ slowly.
Force $F = \frac{GMm}{x^2}$ towards $M$.
External force needed $F_{ext} = \frac{GMm}{x^2}$ (away).
$W = \int_{\infty}^r F_{ext} dx = \int_{\infty}^r \frac{GMm}{x^2} dx$.
$W = GMm [-1/x]_{\infty}^r = -\frac{GMm}{r}$.

related_concepts.name: Negative Sign
related_concepts.definition: Indicates that the force is attractive and the system is bound.

subject: Physics
title: Newton's Law of Gravitation
description: Force of attraction between two point masses. \(F\)=force, \(G\)=gravitational constant \(=6.67\times10^{-11}\,\text{N m}^2\text{kg}^{-2}\), \(m_1,m_2\)=masses, \(r\)=separation.

subject: Physics
title: Gravitational Field (vector)
description: Field intensity due to a point mass, directed toward the mass. \(\vec{E}\)=field per unit mass, \(M\)=source mass, \(r\)=distance, \(\hat{r}\)=outward unit vector.

subject: Physics
title: Gravitational Potential
description: PE per unit mass at distance \(r\) from mass \(M\). \(V\)=potential, \(M\)=mass, \(r\)=distance; zero at infinity, always negative.

subject: Physics
title: Field-Potential Relation
description: Field is negative gradient of potential. \(E\)=field intensity, \(V\)=gravitational potential, \(r\)=distance.

subject: Physics
title: Variation of g (Latitude/Rotation)
description: Effective gravity reduced by Earth's rotation. \(g_\lambda\)=effective \(g\) at latitude \(\lambda\), \(\omega\)=angular speed of Earth, \(R\)=Earth's radius. Max drop at equator (\(\lambda=0\)), zero at poles.

subject: Physics
title: Acceleration g in terms of density
description: Surface gravity from mean density. \(g\)=acceleration, \(R\)=planet radius, \(\rho\)=mean density, \(G\)=grav. constant.

subject: Physics
title: Total Energy in Orbit
description: Total mechanical energy of a satellite in circular orbit (negative = bound). \(E\)=total energy, \(M\)=planet mass, \(m\)=satellite mass, \(r\)=orbital radius.
derivation:
KE \(= \tfrac{1}{2}mv_o^2 = \tfrac{GMm}{2r}\)
PE \(U = -\tfrac{GMm}{r}\)
\(E = KE + U = \tfrac{GMm}{2r} - \tfrac{GMm}{r} = -\tfrac{GMm}{2r}\)

subject: Physics
title: KE & PE of Satellite
description: Energy components for circular orbit; note \(U = -2K\) and \(E = -K\). \(K\)=kinetic energy, \(U\)=potential energy, \(r\)=orbital radius.

subject: Physics
title: Time Period of Satellite
description: Period of a circular orbit of radius \(r\). \(T\)=period, \(M\)=planet mass, \(r\)=orbital radius; for low orbit near surface \(r\approx R\).

subject: Physics
title: Escape vs Orbital Velocity
description: Escape speed is \(\sqrt{2}\) times the orbital speed at the same radius. \(v_e\)=escape velocity, \(v_o\)=orbital velocity.

subject: Physics
title: Escape Velocity (g form)
description: Escape speed from a planet's surface in terms of surface gravity. \(v_e\)=escape velocity, \(g\)=surface gravity, \(R\)=planet radius. For Earth \(\approx 11.2\,\text{km/s}\).

subject: Physics
title: Height of Satellite (from T)
description: Orbital height for a given period (used for geostationary orbit). \(h\)=height above surface, \(T\)=period, \(M\)=Earth mass, \(R\)=Earth radius.

subject: Physics
title: Geostationary Orbit
description: Satellite period equals Earth's rotation; stays fixed above equator. \(T\)=24 h, \(r\)=orbital radius from Earth's centre, height \(\approx 36000\,\text{km}\).

subject: Physics
title: Kepler's Second Law
description: Areal velocity is constant (law of areas), from conservation of angular momentum. \(dA/dt\)=areal velocity, \(L\)=angular momentum, \(m\)=planet mass.

subject: Physics
title: Kepler's First Law
description: Orbit is an ellipse with Sun at one focus. \(r\)=Sun-planet distance, \(a\)=semi-major axis, \(e\)=eccentricity, \(\theta\)=true anomaly.

subject: Physics
title: Velocity at Perihelion/Aphelion
description: Conservation of angular momentum at the two apses of an elliptical orbit. \(v_p,r_p\)=speed & distance at perihelion (nearest), \(v_a,r_a\)=at aphelion (farthest).

subject: Physics
title: Field Inside Solid Sphere
description: Gravitational field inside a uniform solid sphere grows linearly with depth-radius. \(E\)=field, \(M\)=total mass, \(R\)=sphere radius, \(r\)=distance from centre (\(r<R\)).

subject: Physics
title: Potential Inside Solid Sphere
description: Potential inside a uniform solid sphere. \(V\)=potential, \(M\)=mass, \(R\)=radius, \(r\)=distance from centre (\(r<R\)); centre value \(=-\tfrac{3GM}{2R}\).

subject: Physics
title: Self Energy of Sphere
description: Gravitational self (binding) energy of a uniform solid sphere. \(U\)=self energy, \(M\)=total mass, \(R\)=radius.

subject: Physics
title: g on Other Planet
description: Ratio of surface gravity of a planet to Earth. \(g_p,g_e\)=surface gravities, \(M\)=mass, \(R\)=radius; subscripts \(p\)=planet, \(e\)=Earth.

subject: Physics
title: Weightlessness in Orbit
description: In a freely orbiting satellite, gravity provides exactly the centripetal force, so apparent weight (normal reaction) is zero. \(N\)=normal/contact force, \(g_{eff}\)=effective gravity felt.

subject: Physics
title: SHM Displacement
description: Position in Simple Harmonic Motion.
derivation:
From differential equation $\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} + \omega^2 x = 0$.
General solution is sinusoidal.
$A$ is amplitude (max displacement).
$\omega$ is angular frequency (rate of phase change).
$\phi$ is initial phase (at $t=0$).

related_concepts.name: Phase Constant
related_concepts.definition: Determines the starting position and direction of motion at $t=0$.

subject: Physics
title: SHM Velocity
description: Velocity as function of position.
derivation:
$v = \frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(A \cos(\omega t))$.
$v = -A\omega \sin(\omega t)$.
Using $\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta = 1$:
$\sin(\omega t) = \sqrt{1 - \cos^2(\omega t)} = \sqrt{1 - (x/A)^2}$.
$v = -A\omega \sqrt{\frac{A^2-x^2}{A^2}} = \pm \omega \sqrt{A^2-x^2}$

related_concepts.name: Mean Position
related_concepts.definition: Position where net force is zero and velocity is maximum ($v_{max} = A\omega$).

subject: Physics
title: SHM Acceleration
description: Acceleration is proportional to displacement.
derivation:
$a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(-A\omega \sin(\omega t))$.
$a = -A\omega^2 \cos(\omega t)$.
Since $x = A \cos(\omega t)$:
$a = -\omega^2 x$

related_concepts.name: Restoring Force
related_concepts.definition: Force always directed towards equilibrium ($F = ma = -m\omega^2 x = -kx$).

subject: Physics
title: Time Period (Spring)
description: Mass $m$ on spring $k$.
derivation:
Restoring force $F = -kx$.
Newton's Law $F = ma$.
$ma = -kx \implies a = -\frac{k}{m} x$.
Compare with SHM eq $a = -\omega^2 x$:
$\omega^2 = k/m \implies \omega = \sqrt{k/m}$.
$T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}$

related_concepts.name: Inertia Factor
related_concepts.definition: Mass ($m$) represents inertia; Spring constant ($k$) represents stiffness.

subject: Physics
title: Simple Pendulum
description: Valid for small angles.
derivation:
Restoring torque $\tau = -mgL \sin \theta$.
For small $\theta$, $\sin \theta \approx \theta$.
$\tau = -mgL \theta = I \alpha$.
$mL^2 \alpha = -mgL \theta \implies \alpha = -\frac{g}{L} \theta$.
Compare with $\alpha = -\omega^2 \theta$:
$\omega = \sqrt{g/L} \implies T = 2\pi \sqrt{L/g}$

related_concepts.name: Seconds Pendulum
related_concepts.definition: A pendulum with a time period of exactly 2 seconds.

subject: Physics
title: Springs in Series
description: Force is same, extension adds up.
derivation:
Total extension $x = x_1 + x_2$.
Force $F$ is same in both springs.
$x_1 = F/k_1, x_2 = F/k_2$.
$x = F(\frac{1}{k_1} + \frac{1}{k_2})$.
Since $x = F/k_{eq}$:
$\frac{1}{k_{eq}} = \frac{1}{k_1} + \frac{1}{k_2}$

related_concepts.name: Effective Stiffness
related_concepts.definition: Series connection reduces overall stiffness (softer system).

subject: Physics
title: Springs in Parallel
description: Extension is same, force adds up.
derivation:
Both springs extend by same amount $x$.
Total force $F = F_1 + F_2$.
$F_1 = k_1 x, F_2 = k_2 x$.
$F = (k_1 + k_2)x$.
Since $F = k_{eq} x$:
$k_{eq} = k_1 + k_2$

related_concepts.name: Effective Stiffness
related_concepts.definition: Parallel connection increases overall stiffness (stiffer system).

subject: Physics
title: Total Energy in SHM
description: Constant sum of Kinetic and Potential energy.
derivation:
$K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2 \sin^2(\omega t)$.
$U = \frac{1}{2}kx^2 = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2 \cos^2(\omega t)$.
$E = K + U = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2 (\sin^2 + \cos^2)$.
$E = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2$

related_concepts.name: Conservation of Mechanical Energy
related_concepts.definition: In ideal SHM (no damping), energy oscillates between K and U but total remains constant.

subject: Physics
title: Compound Pendulum
description: Physical pendulum time period.
derivation:
Restoring torque about pivot $\tau = -mgd \sin \theta$.
$I \alpha = -mgd \theta$ (small angle).
$\alpha = -\frac{mgd}{I} \theta$.
$\omega^2 = \frac{mgd}{I}$.
$T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{I}{mgd}}$

related_concepts.name: Radius of Gyration
related_concepts.definition: Distance $k$ such that $I = mk^2$. Used to simplify the formula.

subject: Physics
title: Damped Amplitude
description: Decay of amplitude due to damping.
derivation:
Damping force $F_d = -bv$.
Equation: $ma + bv + kx = 0$.
Solution form is $x(t) = A_0 e^{-bt/2m} \cos(\omega' t + \phi)$.
The amplitude term decays exponentially.

related_concepts.name: Critical Damping
related_concepts.definition: Condition ($b = 2\sqrt{mk}$) where system returns to equilibrium fastest without oscillating.

subject: Physics
title: Torsional Pendulum
description: Oscillation of a body suspended by a wire. $C$: Torsional constant.
derivation:
Restoring torque $\tau = -C \theta$ (Hooke's Law for torsion).
Equation: $I \alpha = -C \theta \implies \alpha = -\frac{C}{I} \theta$.
Compare with SHM $\alpha = -\omega^2 \theta$.
$\omega = \sqrt{C/I}$.
$T = 2\pi / \omega$.

related_concepts.name: Torsional Constant
related_concepts.definition: Torque required to twist the wire by 1 radian ($C = \frac{\pi \eta r^4}{2l}$).

subject: Physics
title: Angular Frequency
description: Relates angular frequency to period, frequency and spring constant. \(\omega\)=angular frequency (rad/s), \(T\)=time period, \(f\)=frequency, \(k\)=force constant, \(m\)=mass.

subject: Physics
title: SHM Velocity (time form)
description: Velocity as an explicit function of time in SHM. \(A\)=amplitude, \(\omega\)=angular frequency, \(\phi\)=phase constant, \(v_{max}=A\omega\).

subject: Physics
title: SHM Acceleration (time form)
description: Acceleration as an explicit function of time in SHM. \(A\)=amplitude, \(\omega\)=angular frequency, \(a_{max}=A\omega^2\) at extremes.

subject: Physics
title: Restoring Force in SHM
description: Defining condition of SHM: force proportional and opposite to displacement. \(k\)=force constant, \(x\)=displacement, \(m\)=mass, \(\omega^2 = k/m\).

subject: Physics
title: SHM Differential Equation
description: The governing equation of motion for any SHM. \(x\)=displacement, \(\omega\)=angular frequency. Any system reducible to this form executes SHM.

subject: Physics
title: Kinetic Energy in SHM
description: Kinetic energy at displacement \(x\). \(m\)=mass, \(\omega\)=angular frequency, \(A\)=amplitude, \(x\)=displacement. Maximum at mean position \((x=0)\).

subject: Physics
title: Potential Energy in SHM
description: Elastic potential energy at displacement \(x\). \(m\)=mass, \(\omega\)=angular frequency, \(x\)=displacement, \(k=m\omega^2\). Maximum at extremes.

subject: Physics
title: KE = PE Position
description: Displacement where kinetic and potential energy are equal in SHM. \(A\)=amplitude. At this point each equals half the total energy.

subject: Physics
title: Average KE & PE over Time
description: Time-averaged kinetic and potential energy over one full cycle. \(m\)=mass, \(\omega\)=angular frequency, \(A\)=amplitude. Each equals half the total energy.

subject: Physics
title: Frequency of KE/PE Oscillation
description: KE and PE in SHM oscillate at twice the frequency of displacement. \(f\)=frequency of displacement, \(\omega\)=angular frequency of motion.

subject: Physics
title: Spring with Mass
description: Period of a spring-mass system accounting for spring's own mass. \(m\)=attached mass, \(m_s\)=spring mass, \(k\)=force constant. Effective mass adds \(m_s/3\).

subject: Physics
title: Cut Spring Constant
description: Spring constant rises when a spring is cut shorter. \(k\)=original constant of length \(\ell\), \(k'\)=constant of piece length \(\ell'\); cut into \(n\) equal parts gives \(nk\) each.

subject: Physics
title: Seconds Pendulum
description: Pendulum with a 2 s period (1 s per swing). \(L\)=length \(\approx 0.994\) m at \(g=9.8\). Each one-way swing takes one second.

subject: Physics
title: Pendulum in Lift
description: Pendulum period inside an accelerating lift. \(L\)=length, \(g\)=gravity, \(a\)=lift acceleration; use \(g+a\) (up), \(g-a\) (down), and effective \(g_{eff}\) for free fall \(\to\) no oscillation.

subject: Physics
title: Pendulum in Accelerating Frame
description: Pendulum in a horizontally accelerating vehicle. \(L\)=length, \(g\)=gravity, \(a\)=horizontal acceleration; bob settles at angle \(\theta=\tan^{-1}(a/g)\) from vertical.

subject: Physics
title: Pendulum with Charge in Field
description: Charged pendulum bob in a vertical electric field. \(q\)=charge, \(E\)=field, \(m\)=mass; force \(qE\) adds to or opposes gravity depending on direction.

subject: Physics
title: Angular SHM
description: Rotational analogue of SHM with angular restoring torque. \(\tau\)=torque, \(C\)=torsional constant, \(\theta\)=angular displacement, \(\theta_0\)=angular amplitude.

subject: Physics
title: Phase Difference (x, v, a)
visual_data: v \text{ leads } x \text{ by } \frac{\pi}{2}, \quad a \text{ leads } x \text{ by } \pi
description: Phase relationships among displacement, velocity and acceleration in SHM. Velocity is ahead of displacement by \(\pi/2\); acceleration is opposite (\(\pi\)) to displacement.

subject: Physics
title: SHM v-x Ellipse Relation
description: Velocity-displacement relation traces an ellipse in phase space. \(v\)=velocity, \(x\)=displacement, \(A\)=amplitude, \(\omega\)=angular frequency.

subject: Physics
title: Time for Mean to Extreme
description: Standard SHM transit times starting from mean position. \(T\)=period; \(0\to A/2\) takes \(T/12\), \(0\to A/\sqrt{2}\) takes \(T/8\), \(0\to A\sqrt{3}/2\) takes \(T/6\).

subject: Physics
title: Floating Cylinder SHM
description: Vertical bobbing of a floating cylinder displaced from equilibrium. \(L\)=cylinder length, \(\rho\)=cylinder density, \(\rho_\ell\)=liquid density, \(g\)=gravity.

subject: Physics
title: Tunnel Through Earth
description: SHM of a body dropped in a tunnel through Earth's center. \(R\)=Earth's radius, \(g\)=surface gravity. Period is independent of tunnel orientation.

subject: Physics
title: Damped SHM Frequency
description: Angular frequency of a lightly damped oscillator. \(k\)=force constant, \(m\)=mass, \(b\)=damping constant; valid while \(b^2 < 4mk\) (underdamped).

subject: Physics
title: Damped Energy Decay
description: Mechanical energy of a damped oscillator decays exponentially. \(E_0\)=initial energy, \(b\)=damping constant, \(m\)=mass, \(t\)=time. Decays twice as fast as amplitude.

subject: Physics
title: Resonance Condition
description: Amplitude of forced oscillation peaks when driving frequency equals natural frequency. \(\omega_0\)=natural angular frequency, \(k\)=force constant, \(m\)=mass.

subject: Physics
title: Two Perpendicular SHMs (same f)
description: Lissajous figure from two perpendicular SHMs of equal frequency. \(A,B\)=amplitudes, \(\phi\)=phase difference; \(\phi=0\) gives a line, \(\phi=\pi/2\) an ellipse.

subject: Physics
title: Superposition Same-Frequency SHM
description: Resultant amplitude of two parallel SHMs of equal frequency. \(A_1,A_2\)=component amplitudes, \(\phi\)=phase difference between them.

subject: Physics
title: Equilibrium Stretch in SHM
description: Static extension of a vertical spring sets its period. \(x_0\)=equilibrium stretch, \(m\)=mass, \(g\)=gravity, \(k\)=force constant.

subject: Physics
title: Photoelectric Equation
description: Einstein's photoelectric equation.
derivation:
Based on Conservation of Energy.
Photon Energy = Work Function + Kinetic Energy.
$E = \Phi + K_{max}$.
$h\nu = \Phi + K_{max}$.
$K_{max} = h\nu - \Phi$

related_concepts.name: Work Function
related_concepts.definition: Minimum energy required to eject an electron from a metal surface.

subject: Physics
title: Stopping Potential
description: Retarding potential to stop electrons.
derivation:
Work done by stopping potential $V_s$ on electron equals its max kinetic energy.
$W = \Delta K \implies -eV_s = 0 - K_{max}$.
$K_{max} = eV_s$.
Substituting into Einstein's equation:
$eV_s = h\nu - \Phi$

related_concepts.name: Threshold Frequency
related_concepts.definition: Minimum frequency $\nu_0$ required for photo-emission ($\Phi = h\nu_0$).

subject: Physics
title: De Broglie Wavelength
description: Wave nature of matter.
derivation:
For a photon, $E = h\nu = hc/\lambda$ and $E = pc$.
So $pc = hc/\lambda \implies \lambda = h/p$.
De Broglie proposed this holds for matter too.
$\lambda = \frac{h}{mv} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$

related_concepts.name: Davisson-Germer Experiment
related_concepts.definition: Experiment that proved the wave nature of electrons via diffraction.

subject: Physics
title: X-Ray Cut-off Wavelength
description: Minimum wavelength of continuous X-ray spectrum (Duane-Hunt Law).
derivation:
Conservation of Energy:
The maximum energy of an X-ray photon comes from the complete loss of kinetic energy of an incident electron.
Electron KE gained from voltage $V$ is $K = eV$.
Max Photon energy $E_{max} = h\nu_{max} = hc/\lambda_{min}$.
$eV = \frac{hc}{\lambda_{min}}$.
$\lambda_{min} = \frac{hc}{eV}$.

related_concepts.name: Bremsstrahlung
related_concepts.definition: "Braking radiation" produced when high-speed electrons decelerate upon hitting the target.

subject: Physics
title: Threshold Frequency & Wavelength
description: Minimum frequency/maximum wavelength of light that can eject photoelectrons. \(\nu_0\)=threshold frequency, \(\lambda_0\)=threshold (cut-off) wavelength, \(\Phi\)=work function, \(h\)=Planck's constant, \(c\)=speed of light.
derivation:
Photoemission starts when \(K_{max}=0\)
From \(h
u - \Phi = K_{max}\), set \(K_{max}=0\)
\(	herefore h
u_0 = \Phi \Rightarrow 
u_0 =  rac{\Phi}{h}\)
Using \(
u_0 = c/\lambda_0\) gives \(\lambda_0 =  rac{hc}{\Phi}\)

related_concepts.name: Work function
related_concepts.definition: Minimum energy needed to eject an electron from a metal surface; \(\Phi = h\nu_0\). Lower work function metals (Cs, K) emit even with visible light.

related_concepts.name: No-emission rule
related_concepts.definition: If incident frequency \(\nu<\nu_0\) (or \(\lambda>\lambda_0\)), no photoelectrons are emitted regardless of intensity.

subject: Physics
title: Max Photoelectron Speed
description: Maximum speed of emitted photoelectrons. \(v_{max}\)=max electron speed, \(h\nu\)=photon energy, \(\Phi\)=work function, \(m\)=electron mass, \(e\)=electron charge, \(V_s\)=stopping potential.
derivation:
\(K_{max}=\tfrac{1}{2}mv_{max}^2 = h\nu-\Phi\)
\(\Rightarrow v_{max}=\sqrt{\dfrac{2(h\nu-\Phi)}{m}}\)
Since \(eV_s=K_{max}\), also \(v_{max}=\sqrt{\dfrac{2eV_s}{m}}\)

subject: Physics
title: Photon Energy & Momentum
description: Energy and momentum carried by a single photon. \(E\)=photon energy, \(p\)=photon momentum, \(\nu\)=frequency, \(\lambda\)=wavelength, \(h\)=Planck's constant, \(c\)=speed of light.

related_concepts.name: Rest mass zero
related_concepts.definition: A photon has zero rest mass but nonzero momentum \(p=E/c\), consistent with relativistic \(E=pc\) for massless particles.

related_concepts.name: Energy in eV
related_concepts.definition: \(E(\text{eV}) = \dfrac{1240}{\lambda(\text{nm})}\) — a fast shortcut for converting wavelength to photon energy.

subject: Physics
title: Photon Flux (Photons per Second)
description: Number of photons emitted per second by a source of power P. \(n\)=photons per second, \(P\)=source power (or beam power), \(h\nu\)=energy per photon, \(\lambda\)=wavelength, \(c\)=speed of light.
derivation:
Power = (energy per photon) \(\times\) (photons per second)
\(P = (h\nu)\,n \Rightarrow n = \dfrac{P}{h\nu} = \dfrac{P\lambda}{hc}\)

subject: Physics
title: Radiation Pressure / Force of Photon Beam
description: Force exerted by a photon beam on a surface. \(F\)=force, \(P\)=beam power incident, \(c\)=speed of light; factor 2 for a perfectly reflecting surface (normal incidence).
derivation:
Momentum delivered per second = force
Absorbed: \(F=\dfrac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}=\dfrac{P/c}{1}=\dfrac{P}{c}\)
Reflected: momentum reverses, \(\Delta p\) doubles \(\Rightarrow F=\dfrac{2P}{c}\)

subject: Physics
title: de Broglie Wavelength via Kinetic Energy
description: Matter wavelength of a non-relativistic particle from its kinetic energy. \(\lambda\)=de Broglie wavelength, \(h\)=Planck's constant, \(m\)=mass, \(K\)=kinetic energy of particle.
derivation:
\(K=\dfrac{p^2}{2m} \Rightarrow p=\sqrt{2mK}\)
Substitute in \(\lambda=\dfrac{h}{p}\)
\(\therefore \lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}\)

subject: Physics
title: Electron Wavelength Shortcut
description: Fast formula for de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through V volts. \(\lambda\)=wavelength in angstrom, \(V\)=accelerating potential in volts.
derivation:
From \(\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m_e eV}}\)
Substitute \(h,m_e,e\) and convert to angstrom
\(\therefore \lambda \approx \dfrac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\,\mathring{A}\) (often rounded to 12.3)

subject: Physics
title: Stopping Potential vs Frequency
description: Linear plot of stopping potential against frequency; slope gives h/e. \(V_s\)=stopping potential, \(\nu\)=incident frequency, \(h\)=Planck's constant, \(e\)=electron charge, \(\Phi\)=work function.

related_concepts.name: Slope = h/e
related_concepts.definition: The \(V_s\) vs \(\nu\) graph is a straight line of slope \(h/e\), identical for all metals — a method to determine Planck's constant.

related_concepts.name: Intercepts
related_concepts.definition: x-intercept is the threshold frequency \(\nu_0\); y-intercept (extended) is \(-\Phi/e\).

subject: Physics
title: Photocurrent & Saturation Current
description: Photocurrent depends on intensity (photon rate), not frequency. \(I\)=photocurrent, \(i_{sat}\)=saturation current, \(n\)=photons incident per second, \(e\)=electron charge, \(\eta\)=quantum efficiency (electrons emitted per incident photon).

related_concepts.name: Saturation
related_concepts.definition: At high enough positive collector voltage, all emitted electrons are collected; current saturates and depends only on intensity.

related_concepts.name: Stopping point
related_concepts.definition: Stopping potential \(V_s\) (where current = 0) depends only on frequency and work function, NOT on intensity.

subject: Physics
title: Davisson-Germer / Bragg Condition
description: Electron diffraction confirming wave nature; Bragg condition for constructive interference from crystal planes. \(d\)=interplanar spacing, \(\theta\)=glancing (Bragg) angle, \(n\)=order of diffraction, \(\lambda\)=electron de Broglie wavelength.

related_concepts.name: Experimental verification
related_concepts.definition: Davisson-Germer scattered 54 eV electrons off nickel; the measured \(\lambda\approx1.65\,\mathring{A}\) matched de Broglie's prediction, confirming matter waves.

subject: Physics
title: Moseley's Law
description: X-ray frequency relation to Atomic Number.
derivation:
Based on Bohr model for X-ray transitions.
Energy $\Delta E \propto (Z_{eff})^2$.
Frequency $\nu \propto \Delta E \propto (Z-b)^2$.
Taking square root:
$\sqrt{\nu} \propto (Z-b)$

related_concepts.name: Screening Constant
related_concepts.definition: Constant $b$ that accounts for the repulsion from inner shell electrons.

subject: Physics
title: Bohr Radius
description: Radius of nth orbit in hydrogen-like atom.
derivation:
Force balance: $\frac{mv^2}{r} = \frac{kZe^2}{r^2}$.
Quantization: $mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi}$.
Solve for $v$ in 2nd eq and substitute into 1st.
$r = \frac{n^2 h^2}{4\pi^2 m k Z e^2}$.
Calculating constants yields $r_n \propto n^2/Z$.

related_concepts.name: Bohr's Postulates
related_concepts.definition: Electrons orbit in stable stationary states without radiating energy.

subject: Physics
title: Bohr Energy Levels
description: Total energy of electron in nth orbit.
derivation:
Total Energy $E = K + U$.
$U = -\frac{kZe^2}{r}$ and $K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{kZe^2}{2r}$ (from force balance).
$E = -\frac{kZe^2}{2r}$.
Substitute expression for $r \propto n^2/Z$:
$E \propto -\frac{Z^2}{n^2}$.

related_concepts.name: Ionization Energy
related_concepts.definition: Energy required to remove an electron from the ground state ($n=1$) to infinity ($E=0$).

subject: Physics
title: Rydberg Formula
description: Wavelength of emitted photon during transition.
derivation:
Energy difference $\Delta E = E_{n2} - E_{n1}$.
$\Delta E = 13.6 Z^2 (\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2})$.
Photon energy $hc/\lambda = \Delta E$.
$\frac{1}{\lambda} = \frac{13.6 \text{ eV}}{hc} Z^2 (...)$.
The constant term is Rydberg constant $R \approx 1.097 \times 10^7 m^{-1}$.

related_concepts.name: Spectral Series
related_concepts.definition: Lyman ($n_1=1$), Balmer ($n_1=2$), Paschen ($n_1=3$), etc.

subject: Physics
title: Distance of Closest Approach
description: Rutherford scattering parameter.
derivation:
Conservation of Energy at closest approach (velocity becomes zero momentarily).
Initial Kinetic Energy = Final Potential Energy.
$K_\alpha = \frac{k (2e) (Ze)}{r_0}$.
$K_\alpha = \frac{2kZe^2}{r_0}$.
$r_0 = \frac{2kZe^2}{K_\alpha}$.

related_concepts.name: Impact Parameter
related_concepts.definition: Perpendicular distance of the velocity vector of the alpha particle from the center of the nucleus.

subject: Physics
title: Bohr's Quantisation of Angular Momentum
visual_data: L = m v_n r_n = \frac{n h}{2 \pi} = n \hbar
description: Bohr's postulate: angular momentum is quantised in integer multiples of \(h/2\pi\). \(L\)=angular momentum, \(m\)=electron mass, \(v_n\)=speed in nth orbit, \(r_n\)=radius of nth orbit, \(n\)=principal quantum number, \(h\)=Planck's constant, \(\hbar = h/2\pi\).

subject: Physics
title: Velocity in nth Orbit
description: Speed of electron in the nth Bohr orbit; gives \(v_1 = \alpha c \approx c/137\). \(v_n\)=orbital speed, \(Z\)=atomic number, \(n\)=orbit number, \(k=1/4\pi\varepsilon_0\), \(e\)=electronic charge, \(h\)=Planck's constant.

subject: Physics
title: Kinetic, Potential & Total Energy Relations
description: Virial relations linking kinetic, potential and total energy in a Bohr orbit. \(K\)=kinetic energy, \(U\)=potential energy, \(E\)=total energy (\(E = -13.6\,Z^2/n^2\) eV). Note \(U = -2K\) and \(E = -K\).

subject: Physics
title: Time Period & Frequency of Revolution
description: Orbital period and revolution frequency of the electron in the nth orbit. \(T_n\)=time period, \(f_n\)=frequency of revolution, \(r_n\)=orbit radius, \(v_n\)=orbital speed, \(n\)=orbit number, \(Z\)=atomic number.

subject: Physics
title: Rydberg Constant Value
description: Theoretical expression and value of the Rydberg constant for hydrogen (infinite-mass nucleus). \(R\)=Rydberg constant, \(m\)=electron mass, \(e\)=charge, \(\varepsilon_0\)=permittivity of free space, \(h\)=Planck's constant, \(c\)=speed of light.

subject: Physics
title: Series Limit Wavelength
description: Shortest wavelength (series limit) of a spectral series, obtained when \(n_2 \to \infty\). \(\lambda_{\min}\)=series-limit wavelength, \(n_1\)=lower level (1 Lyman, 2 Balmer, 3 Paschen), \(R\)=Rydberg constant, \(Z\)=atomic number.

subject: Physics
title: Number of Spectral Lines Emitted
description: Total number of distinct spectral lines when an electron de-excites from level \(n\) to the ground state. \(N\)=number of emission lines, \(n\)=initial principal quantum number. (From \(n\) to \(m\): \(N=\frac{(n-m)(n-m+1)}{2}\).)

subject: Physics
title: Ionisation & Excitation Energy
description: Energy to remove the electron from level \(n\) to infinity, and to lift it between levels. \(E_{ion}\)=ionisation energy from level \(n\) (13.6 eV for H ground state), \(E_{exc}\)=excitation energy, \(Z\)=atomic number, \(n\)=quantum number.

subject: Physics
title: Wavelength of Hα Line (Balmer)
description: First (red) line of the Balmer series, the \(3 \to 2\) transition in hydrogen. \(\lambda\)=wavelength of H\(\alpha\), \(R\)=Rydberg constant. The most frequently asked visible-spectrum value.

subject: Physics
title: Reduced Mass Correction
description: Finite nuclear mass correction to energy levels and Rydberg constant (e.g. deuterium, positronium). \(\mu\)=reduced mass, \(m\)=electron mass, \(M\)=nuclear mass, \(R_M\)=corrected Rydberg constant, \(R_\infty\)=infinite-mass value.

subject: Physics
title: de Broglie Condition for Bohr Orbit
description: Bohr's quantisation reinterpreted: orbit circumference holds an integer number of de Broglie wavelengths (standing wave). \(r_n\)=orbit radius, \(n\)=number of wavelengths, \(\lambda\)=de Broglie wavelength, \(h\)=Planck's constant, \(m\)=electron mass, \(v_n\)=orbital speed.

subject: Physics
title: Magnetic Field & Moment at Nucleus
visual_data: B = \frac{\mu_0 e f}{2 r_n}, \quad M = \frac{n e h}{4 \pi m}
description: Magnetic field at the nucleus due to orbital current, and the orbital magnetic moment (Bohr magneton multiples). \(B\)=field at nucleus, \(\mu_0\)=permeability, \(f\)=revolution frequency, \(r_n\)=orbit radius, \(M\)=magnetic moment, \(n\)=orbit number, \(e\),\(m\)=electron charge & mass.

subject: Physics
title: Photon Energy of Transition
description: Bohr's frequency condition: emitted/absorbed photon energy equals the level gap. \(h\nu\)=photon energy, \(E_{n}\)=level energies, \(Z\)=atomic number, \(n_1\)=lower level, \(n_2\)=upper level. Use \(\lambda(\text{nm}) = 1240/E(\text{eV})\).

subject: Physics
title: Nuclear Radius
description: Size of nucleus depends on Mass Number $A$.
derivation:
Nuclear density is roughly constant.
Volume $V \propto A$ (Mass Number).
$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \propto A$.
$R^3 \propto A \implies R \propto A^{1/3}$.
$R = R_0 A^{1/3}$

related_concepts.name: Femtometer (Fermi)
related_concepts.definition: Unit of length $1 fm = 10^{-15} m$, typical scale of nuclei.

subject: Physics
title: Mass-Energy Equivalence
description: Energy released due to mass defect.
derivation:
Derived from Special Relativity.
Mass and energy are interchangeable.
When nucleons form a nucleus, mass decreases (Mass Defect $\Delta m$).
This lost mass is released as Binding Energy.

related_concepts.name: Mass Defect
related_concepts.definition: Difference between mass of constituent nucleons and the actual nucleus mass.

subject: Physics
title: Radioactive Decay Law
description: Exponential decay of active nuclei.
derivation:
Rate of decay is proportional to number of nuclei present.
$\frac{dN}{dt} = -\lambda N$.
$\frac{dN}{N} = -\lambda dt$.
Integrate from $N_0$ to $N$: $\ln(N/N_0) = -\lambda t$.
$N = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$

related_concepts.name: Decay Constant
related_concepts.definition: Probability of decay per unit time for a nucleus ($\lambda$).

subject: Physics
title: Half-Life
description: Time for number of nuclei to reduce to half.
derivation:
Set $N = N_0 / 2$ in decay equation.
$N_0 / 2 = N_0 e^{-\lambda T_{1/2}}$.
$1/2 = e^{-\lambda T_{1/2}} \implies 2 = e^{\lambda T_{1/2}}$.
Take $\ln$: $\ln 2 = \lambda T_{1/2}$.
$T_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{\lambda}$

related_concepts.name: Activity
related_concepts.definition: Number of decays per second (Becquerel).

subject: Physics
title: Average Life
description: Mean survival time of a nucleus.
derivation:
Sum of all life times divided by total nuclei.
$\tau = \frac{\int_0^\infty t |dN|}{\int |dN|} = \frac{\int_0^\infty t (\lambda N_0 e^{-\lambda t}) dt}{N_0}$.
Solving integral $\lambda \int t e^{-\lambda t} dt$ gives $1/\lambda$.
$\tau = 1.44 T_{1/2}$

related_concepts.name: Statistical Nature
related_concepts.definition: Radioactivity is random; impossible to predict when a specific nucleus will decay.

subject: Physics
title: Activity
description: Rate of decay.
derivation:
Defined as $A = -\frac{dN}{dt}$.
From decay law: $\frac{d}{dt}(N_0 e^{-\lambda t}) = -\lambda N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$.
$A = \lambda N$.
Also follows $A = A_0 e^{-\lambda t}$.

related_concepts.name: Curie (Ci)
related_concepts.definition: Older unit of activity ($1 Ci = 3.7 \times 10^{10} Bq$).

subject: Physics
title: Q-Value (Alpha Decay)
description: Energy released in decay.
derivation:
Reaction: $X \rightarrow Y + \alpha$.
Mass of reactants: $m_X$.
Mass of products: $m_Y + m_\alpha$.
Mass Defect $\Delta m = m_X - (m_Y + m_\alpha)$.
Energy $Q = \Delta m c^2$.

related_concepts.name: Exothermic Reaction
related_concepts.definition: Q > 0 implies energy is released (spontaneous decay).

subject: Physics
title: Parallel Decay Constant
description: Simultaneous decay processes.
derivation:
Rate of decay 1: $(dN/dt)_1 = -\lambda_1 N$.
Rate of decay 2: $(dN/dt)_2 = -\lambda_2 N$.
Total rate: $dN/dt = -(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2)N$.
Effective constant $\lambda_{eff} = \lambda_1 + \lambda_2$.

related_concepts.name: Branching Ratio
related_concepts.definition: Fraction of decays going via a specific mode (e.g., $\lambda_1 / \lambda_{eff}$).

subject: Physics
title: Binding Energy
description: Energy required to disassemble a nucleus.
derivation:
Mass of nucleus $M_{nuc}$ is less than sum of parts.
$\Delta m = [Z m_p + (A-Z) m_n] - M_{nuc}$.
$E_b = \Delta m \times 931.5$ MeV (if mass in amu).
Binding Energy per nucleon ($E_{bn} = E_b/A$) determines stability.

related_concepts.name: Iron-56
related_concepts.definition: The most stable isotope with the highest binding energy per nucleon (~8.8 MeV).

subject: Physics
title: Nuclear Density
description: Density of nuclear matter, independent of mass number A. \(m\)=mass of one nucleon, \(R_0 \approx 1.2\) fm, \(\rho\)=nuclear density.
derivation:
Mass \(= A m\), Volume \(= \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3 A\)
\(\rho = \frac{A m}{\frac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3 A} = \frac{3m}{4\pi R_0^3}\)
A cancels, so \(\rho\) is constant for all nuclei.

subject: Physics
title: Atomic Mass Unit Energy
description: Energy equivalent of one atomic mass unit, used to convert mass defect to energy. \(u\)=unified atomic mass unit, \(c\)=speed of light.

subject: Physics
title: Mass Defect
description: Mass lost when nucleons bind into a nucleus. \(Z\)=protons, \(A\)=mass number, \(m_p\)=proton mass, \(m_n\)=neutron mass, \(M\)=nuclear mass.

subject: Physics
title: Binding Energy per Nucleon
description: Average energy to remove one nucleon; measures nuclear stability (peak \(\approx 8.8\) MeV near Fe-56). \(E_b\)=total binding energy, \(A\)=mass number.

subject: Physics
title: Binding Energy (in u)
visual_data: E_b = \Delta m \times 931.5 \text{ MeV} \quad (\Delta m \text{ in } u)
description: Quick computation of binding energy when mass defect is given in atomic mass units. \(\Delta m\)=mass defect in \(u\).

subject: Physics
title: Number of Nuclei Remaining (n half-lives)
description: Undecayed nuclei after an integer or fractional number of half-lives. \(N_0\)=initial nuclei, \(n\)=number of half-lives, \(t\)=elapsed time.

subject: Physics
title: Relation: Mean Life & Half-Life
description: Mean (average) life is longer than half-life. \(\tau\)=mean life, \(T_{1/2}\)=half-life.

subject: Physics
title: Activity Decay (in time)
visual_data: A = A_0 e^{-\lambda t} = \lambda N_0 e^{-\lambda t}
description: Activity falls exponentially with the same decay constant as nuclei. \(A_0\)=initial activity, \(\lambda\)=decay constant, \(t\)=time.

subject: Physics
title: Units of Activity (Becquerel & Curie)
description: SI and traditional units of radioactivity. \(1\) Ci is the activity of \(1\) g of radium.

subject: Physics
title: Fraction Remaining & Decayed
description: Fraction of nuclei left and fraction that has decayed at time t. \(N\)=remaining nuclei, \(N_0\)=initial nuclei, \(\lambda\)=decay constant.

subject: Physics
title: Alpha Decay (General)
description: Emission of an alpha particle; mass number drops by 4, atomic number by 2. \(X\)=parent, \(Y\)=daughter, \(_{2}^{4}He\)=alpha particle.

subject: Physics
title: Beta-Minus Decay
description: A neutron converts to a proton, emitting an electron and antineutrino; Z increases by 1. \(\bar{\nu}\)=antineutrino, \(e^-\)=beta particle.

subject: Physics
title: Beta-Plus Decay
description: A proton converts to a neutron, emitting a positron and neutrino; Z decreases by 1. \(\nu\)=neutrino, \(e^+\)=positron.

subject: Physics
title: Q-Value (General Reaction)
description: Energy released in a nuclear reaction; positive Q means exothermic. \(m\)=rest masses, \(\Delta m\)=mass difference in \(u\).

subject: Physics
title: Kinetic Energy of Alpha Particle
description: Share of disintegration energy carried by alpha particle (momentum conservation). \(A\)=parent mass number, \(Q\)=Q-value of alpha decay.
derivation:
By momentum conservation \(p_\alpha = p_Y\)
\(K = \frac{p^2}{2m}\Rightarrow \frac{K_\alpha}{K_Y} = \frac{m_Y}{m_\alpha}\)
\(Q = K_\alpha + K_Y\), with \(m_Y \approx A-4,\ m_\alpha = 4\)
\(K_\alpha = \frac{m_Y}{m_Y + m_\alpha}Q = \frac{A-4}{A}Q\)

subject: Physics
title: Q-Value via Binding Energies
description: Energy released equals increase in total binding energy of products over reactants. \(E_b\)=total binding energy of nuclei involved.

subject: Physics
title: Energy in Fission of U-235
description: Typical induced fission releasing about 200 MeV per event. \(Q \approx 200\) MeV, \(_{0}^{1}n\)=neutron.

subject: Physics
title: Deuterium-Tritium Fusion
description: Standard D-T fusion reaction; releases energy as light nuclei fuse. \(_{1}^{2}H\)=deuterium, \(_{1}^{3}H\)=tritium.

subject: Physics
title: Number of Atoms from Mass
description: Counts nuclei in a sample, needed to find activity. \(m\)=sample mass, \(M\)=molar/atomic mass, \(N_A = 6.022\times10^{23}\)=Avogadro number.

subject: Physics
title: Time from Activity/Number Ratio
description: Age/elapsed time from a measured fall in number or activity. \(N_0,A_0\)=initial values, \(N,A\)=present values, \(\lambda\)=decay constant.

subject: Physics
title: Decay Constant from Half-Life
description: Probability of decay per unit time per nucleus. \(T_{1/2}\)=half-life, \(\lambda\)=decay constant (units s\(^{-1}\)).

subject: Physics
title: Projectile Time of Flight
description: Total time in air.
derivation:
Vertical motion: $u_y = u \sin \theta, a_y = -g$.
At highest point, $v_y = 0$. Time to rise $t_{up}$.
$v_y = u_y - gt \implies 0 = u \sin \theta - g t_{up}$.
$t_{up} = \frac{u \sin \theta}{g}$.
Total time $T = 2 t_{up} = \frac{2u \sin \theta}{g}$

related_concepts.name: Independence of Motion
related_concepts.definition: Horizontal and vertical components of projectile motion are independent.

subject: Physics
title: Projectile Max Height
description: Max vertical displacement.
derivation:
Using kinematic equation $v^2 - u^2 = 2as$ for vertical motion.
At max height $v_y = 0$, $u_y = u \sin \theta$.
$0 - (u \sin \theta)^2 = 2(-g)H$.
$H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$

related_concepts.name: Launch Angle
related_concepts.definition: Height is maximum at $\theta = 90^\circ$.

subject: Physics
title: Projectile Range
description: Horizontal distance covered.
derivation:
Horizontal speed $u_x = u \cos \theta$ (constant).
$R = u_x \times T = (u \cos \theta) \times \frac{2u \sin \theta}{g}$.
$R = \frac{u^2 (2 \sin \theta \cos \theta)}{g}$.
Using $\sin 2\theta = 2 \sin \theta \cos \theta$:
$R = \frac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}$

related_concepts.name: Max Range
related_concepts.definition: Occurs at $45^\circ$. Complementary angles ($\theta, 90-\theta$) give same range.

subject: Physics
title: Equation of Trajectory
description: Path of projectile.
derivation:
Eliminate $t$ from $x$ and $y$ equations.
$x = (u \cos \theta) t \implies t = \frac{x}{u \cos \theta}$.
$y = (u \sin \theta)t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$.
Substitute $t$:
$y = x \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} - \frac{g}{2} (\frac{x}{u \cos \theta})^2$.
$y = x \tan \theta - \frac{gx^2}{2u^2 \cos^2 \theta}$

related_concepts.name: Parabola
related_concepts.definition: Geometric shape of the projectile path ($y = ax - bx^2$).

subject: Physics
title: Trajectory (Range Form)
description: Trajectory equation using Range.
derivation:
Start from $y = x \tan \theta - \frac{gx^2}{2u^2 \cos^2 \theta}$.
Factor out $x \tan \theta$:
$y = x \tan \theta [ 1 - \frac{gx}{2u^2 \cos^2 \theta \tan \theta} ]$.
Simplify fraction: $\frac{gx}{2u^2 \sin \theta \cos \theta} = \frac{x}{R}$.
$y = x \tan \theta (1 - x/R)$

related_concepts.name: Symmetric Path
related_concepts.definition: The trajectory is symmetric about the vertical line $x = R/2$.

subject: Physics
title: Relative Velocity
description: Velocity of A with respect to B.
derivation:
Position vector $\vec{r}_{AB} = \vec{r}_A - \vec{r}_B$.
Differentiating with respect to time:
$\frac{d\vec{r}_{AB}}{dt} = \frac{d\vec{r}_A}{dt} - \frac{d\vec{r}_B}{dt}$.
$\vec{v}_{AB} = \vec{v}_A - \vec{v}_B$

related_concepts.name: Frame of Reference
related_concepts.definition: The coordinate system from which motion is observed (B is the frame here).

subject: Physics
title: River-Boat (Min Dist)
description: Heading to cross directly opposite.
derivation:
To cancel river flow $v_r$, horizontal component of boat velocity must oppose it.
$v_{b,x} = v_b \sin \theta$.
Condition: $v_b \sin \theta = v_r$.
$\sin \theta = v_r / v_b$.
Only possible if boat speed > river speed.

related_concepts.name: Drift
related_concepts.definition: Distance moved downstream. For min distance, drift is zero.

subject: Physics
title: River-Boat (Min Time)
description: Heading to cross fastest.
derivation:
Time to cross $t = \frac{\text{width}}{v_y}$.
$v_y = v_b \cos \theta$ (where $\theta$ is angle with normal).
To minimize $t$, maximize denominator $\cos \theta$.
Max $\cos \theta = 1$ at $\theta = 0$.
Boat must head perpendicular to flow.
$t_{min} = d/v_b$

related_concepts.name: Resultant Velocity
related_concepts.definition: Vector sum of boat and river velocity ($\sqrt{v_b^2 + v_r^2}$).

subject: Physics
title: Rain-Man Problem
description: Velocity of rain w.r.t moving man (Umbrella angle).
derivation:
Rain falls vertically $\vec{v}_r = -v_y \hat{j}$.
Man moves horizontally $\vec{v}_m = v_x \hat{i}$.
Relative velocity $\vec{v}_{rm} = -v_x \hat{i} - v_y \hat{j}$.
Angle to hold umbrella: $\tan \theta = \frac{v_x}{v_y} = \frac{v_{man}}{v_{rain}}$.
(Angle with vertical).

related_concepts.name: Relative Motion
related_concepts.definition: Observation depends on the frame of reference of the observer.

subject: Physics
title: Radius of Curvature (Projectile)
description: Radius of trajectory circle at any point.
derivation:
General formula for curvature $R = v^2 / a_{\perp}$.
$a_{\perp}$ is the component of acceleration perpendicular to velocity.
For projectile, acceleration is always $g$ down.
Component normal to velocity is $g \cos \alpha$ (where $\alpha$ is angle with horizontal).
$R = v^2 / (g \cos \alpha)$.

related_concepts.name: Min Radius
related_concepts.definition: Occurs at highest point where $v$ is min and $\alpha=0$. $R = u^2 \cos^2 \theta / g$.

subject: Physics
title: First Eqn of Motion
description: Velocity after time t for constant acceleration. \(v\)=final velocity, \(u\)=initial velocity, \(a\)=acceleration, \(t\)=time.
derivation:
By definition \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\), constant \(a\).
Integrate: \(\int_u^v dv = \int_0^t a\, dt\).
\(v - u = at\).
\(v = u + at\)

related_concepts.name: Uniform Acceleration
related_concepts.definition: Acceleration that is constant in magnitude and direction; valid condition for all three SUVAT equations.

related_concepts.name: Sign Convention
related_concepts.definition: Take one direction positive; \(a\) is negative (retardation) if it opposes velocity.

subject: Physics
title: Second Eqn of Motion
description: Displacement in time t for constant acceleration. \(s\)=displacement, \(u\)=initial velocity, \(a\)=acceleration, \(t\)=time.
derivation:
\(v = \frac{ds}{dt} = u + at\).
Integrate: \(\int_0^s ds = \int_0^t (u + at)\, dt\).
\(s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\)

related_concepts.name: Displacement vs Distance
related_concepts.definition: \(s\) here is displacement (vector); equals distance only when motion does not reverse.

subject: Physics
title: Third Eqn of Motion
description: Velocity-displacement relation (time-independent). \(v\)=final velocity, \(u\)=initial velocity, \(a\)=acceleration, \(s\)=displacement.
derivation:
Use \(v\frac{dv}{ds} = a\) (since \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{dv}{ds}\frac{ds}{dt}\)).
\(\int_u^v v\, dv = \int_0^s a\, ds\).
\(\frac{v^2 - u^2}{2} = as\).
\(v^2 = u^2 + 2as\)

related_concepts.name: Time Eliminated
related_concepts.definition: Most useful when time is neither given nor asked — links speeds directly to distance.

subject: Physics
title: Distance in nth Second
description: Displacement during the nth second alone (uniform acceleration). \(s_n\)=distance in nth second, \(u\)=initial velocity, \(a\)=acceleration, \(n\)=second number.

related_concepts.name: Units Note
related_concepts.definition: \(s_n\) has units of metre, not m/s, though it is a distance per 1 second interval.

subject: Physics
title: Average Velocity
description: Net displacement per total time. \(\bar{v}\)=average velocity, \(\Delta x\)=displacement, \(\Delta t\)=time interval.

related_concepts.name: Average Speed
related_concepts.definition: Total path length / total time; \(\ge\) magnitude of average velocity.

related_concepts.name: Graphical Meaning
related_concepts.definition: Slope of the chord joining two points on the position-time graph.

subject: Physics
title: Average Velocity (Uniform a)
description: Mean velocity for constant acceleration only. \(u\)=initial velocity, \(v\)=final velocity.
derivation:
For uniform \(a\), velocity varies linearly in time.
Mean of a linear function = average of endpoints.
\(\bar{v} = \frac{u + v}{2}\)

related_concepts.name: Validity
related_concepts.definition: Holds only for constant acceleration; fails if \(a\) varies.

subject: Physics
title: Instantaneous Velocity
description: Velocity at an instant. \(v\)=instantaneous velocity, \(x\)=position, \(t\)=time.

related_concepts.name: Slope of x-t Graph
related_concepts.definition: Equals the tangent slope at that point on the position-time curve.

subject: Physics
title: Instantaneous Acceleration
description: Acceleration at an instant. \(a\)=acceleration, \(v\)=velocity, \(x\)=position, \(t\)=time.

related_concepts.name: Slope of v-t Graph
related_concepts.definition: Equals the tangent slope of the velocity-time curve.

related_concepts.name: Velocity-Displacement Form
related_concepts.definition: \(a = v\frac{dv}{dx}\), useful when \(a\) is given as a function of position.

subject: Physics
title: Displacement from v-t Graph
description: Displacement equals area under the velocity-time graph. \(x\)=displacement, \(v\)=velocity, \(t\)=time.

related_concepts.name: Signed Area
related_concepts.definition: Area below the time axis is negative displacement; for distance use the magnitude.

related_concepts.name: Change in Velocity
related_concepts.definition: Area under a-t graph gives \(\Delta v = \int a\, dt\).

subject: Physics
title: Free Fall: Velocity
description: Body dropped from rest (\(u=0\)). \(v\)=speed, \(g\)=acceleration due to gravity, \(t\)=time, \(h\)=fall height.
derivation:
With \(u=0, a=g\): \(v = u + gt = gt\).
Also \(v^2 = u^2 + 2gh = 2gh\).
\(v = \sqrt{2gh}\)

related_concepts.name: Independent of Mass
related_concepts.definition: In absence of air resistance, all bodies fall with the same \(g\).

subject: Physics
title: Free Fall: Height & Time
description: Distance fallen and time to fall from rest. \(h\)=height, \(g\)=gravity, \(t\)=time.
derivation:
With \(u=0, a=g\): \(h = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = \frac{1}{2}gt^2\).
Solve for \(t\): \(t = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}\)

related_concepts.name: Ratio of Distances
related_concepts.definition: Distances in successive equal time intervals from rest are in ratio \(1:3:5:7\dots\) (Galileo's odd-number rule).

subject: Physics
title: Vertical Throw: Max Height
description: Body thrown straight up with speed u. \(H\)=max height, \(u\)=launch speed, \(g\)=gravity, \(t_{up}\)=time to top.
derivation:
At top \(v=0\). Using \(v^2 = u^2 - 2gH\): \(0 = u^2 - 2gH\).
\(H = \frac{u^2}{2g}\).
Using \(v = u - gt\): \(0 = u - gt_{up} \Rightarrow t_{up} = \frac{u}{g}\)

related_concepts.name: Time Symmetry
related_concepts.definition: Time of ascent equals time of descent; speed on return to launch level equals \(u\).

subject: Physics
title: Horizontal Projectile: Time
description: Object launched horizontally from height h. \(T\)=time of flight, \(h\)=launch height, \(g\)=gravity.
derivation:
Vertical: \(u_y = 0\), so \(h = \frac{1}{2}gT^2\).
Solve: \(T = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}\).
Independent of horizontal speed \(u\)

related_concepts.name: Monkey-Hunter Idea
related_concepts.definition: Time to land depends only on \(h\), not on horizontal launch speed.

subject: Physics
title: Horizontal Projectile: Velocity
description: Speed and direction during horizontal projection. \(v\)=speed at time t, \(u\)=horizontal speed, \(g\)=gravity, \(\phi\)=angle below horizontal.
derivation:
\(v_x = u\) (constant), \(v_y = gt\).
\(v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{u^2 + g^2 t^2}\).
Direction: \(\tan \phi = \frac{v_y}{v_x} = \frac{gt}{u}\)

related_concepts.name: Angle Below Horizontal
related_concepts.definition: \(\phi\) grows with time as vertical speed builds up.

subject: Physics
title: Projectile Velocity at Time t
description: Speed of an oblique projectile at any instant t. \(v\)=speed, \(u\)=launch speed, \(\theta\)=launch angle, \(g\)=gravity, \(t\)=time.
derivation:
\(v_x = u\cos\theta\), \(v_y = u\sin\theta - gt\).
\(v^2 = v_x^2 + v_y^2 = u^2\cos^2\theta + (u\sin\theta - gt)^2\).
Expand: \(v^2 = u^2 - 2ugt\sin\theta + g^2 t^2\)

related_concepts.name: Speed at Top
related_concepts.definition: At the highest point \(v_y = 0\), so the speed reduces to \(u\cos\theta\).

subject: Physics
title: Projectile Components
description: Velocity components of an oblique projectile. \(v_x\)=horizontal velocity (constant), \(v_y\)=vertical velocity, \(u\)=launch speed, \(\theta\)=launch angle, \(g\)=gravity, \(t\)=time.

related_concepts.name: Constant Horizontal
related_concepts.definition: No horizontal force, so \(v_x\) stays \(u\cos\theta\) throughout the flight.

related_concepts.name: Velocity Angle
related_concepts.definition: Instantaneous direction: \(\tan\alpha = v_y / v_x\).

subject: Physics
title: Max Height in Terms of Range
description: Links projectile max height to range and angle. \(H\)=max height, \(R\)=range, \(\theta\)=launch angle.
derivation:
\(H = \frac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}\), \(R = \frac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g} = \frac{2u^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}\).
\(\frac{H}{R} = \frac{\sin^2\theta / 2}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \frac{\tan\theta}{4}\).
\(H = \frac{R\tan\theta}{4}\)

related_concepts.name: At 45 Degrees
related_concepts.definition: When \(\theta = 45^\circ\), \(R = 4H\) (range is four times the max height).

subject: Physics
title: Centripetal Acceleration
description: Radial acceleration in uniform circular motion. \(a_c\)=centripetal acceleration, \(v\)=speed, \(r\)=radius, \(\omega\)=angular velocity.
derivation:
In uniform circular motion the velocity vector turns at rate \(\omega\).
Magnitude of \(\frac{d\vec{v}}{dt}\) is \(v\omega\), directed toward centre.
With \(v = \omega r\): \(a_c = v\omega = \frac{v^2}{r} = \omega^2 r\)

related_concepts.name: Direction
related_concepts.definition: Always points toward the centre; changes velocity's direction, not its magnitude.

related_concepts.name: Angular-Linear Link
related_concepts.definition: \(v = \omega r\) connects linear speed and angular velocity.

subject: Physics
title: Angular Velocity & Period
description: Angular velocity for circular motion. \(\omega\)=angular velocity, \(T\)=time period, \(f\)=frequency, \(v\)=linear speed, \(r\)=radius.

related_concepts.name: Frequency
related_concepts.definition: \(f = 1/T\); number of revolutions per second (Hz).

subject: Physics
title: Total Acceleration (Circular)
description: Net acceleration in non-uniform circular motion. \(a\)=total acceleration, \(a_t\)=tangential acceleration, \(a_c\)=centripetal (radial) acceleration.
derivation:
Tangential part \(a_t = \frac{dv}{dt}\) changes speed.
Radial part \(a_c = \frac{v^2}{r}\) changes direction.
The two are perpendicular, so \(a = \sqrt{a_t^2 + a_c^2}\)

related_concepts.name: Tangential Acceleration
related_concepts.definition: \(a_t = r\alpha\), where \(\alpha\) is angular acceleration; zero in uniform circular motion.

subject: Physics
title: Resultant of Two Velocities
description: Magnitude of vector sum of two velocities at angle. \(v\)=resultant, \(v_1, v_2\)=velocities, \(\theta\)=angle between them.
derivation:
Parallelogram law of vector addition.
\(\vec{v} = \vec{v}_1 + \vec{v}_2\).
\(|\vec{v}|^2 = v_1^2 + v_2^2 + 2v_1 v_2\cos\theta\)

related_concepts.name: Direction of Resultant
related_concepts.definition: \(\tan\beta = \frac{v_2\sin\theta}{v_1 + v_2\cos\theta}\), angle with \(\vec{v}_1\).

subject: Physics
title: Work (Variable Force)
description: Area under Force-Displacement graph.
derivation:
For constant force $W = F \cdot s$.
For variable force, consider small displacement $d\vec{r}$ where $F$ is approx constant.
$dW = \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}$.
Summing all contributions via integration:
$W = \int_{r_1}^{r_2} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}$

related_concepts.name: Dot Product
related_concepts.definition: Scalar product indicating work depends on component of force parallel to displacement.

subject: Physics
title: Work-Energy Theorem
description: Net work equals change in Kinetic Energy.
derivation:
Newton's 2nd Law: $F_{net} = ma = m v \frac{dv}{dx}$.
$W = \int F dx = \int (m v \frac{dv}{dx}) dx = \int_{v_i}^{v_f} m v dv$.
$W = m [\frac{v^2}{2}]_{v_i}^{v_f} = \frac{1}{2}mv_f^2 - \frac{1}{2}mv_i^2$.
$W_{net} = K_f - K_i$

related_concepts.name: Kinetic Energy
related_concepts.definition: Energy possessed by an object due to its motion ($K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$).

subject: Physics
title: Instantaneous Power
description: Rate of doing work.
derivation:
Power $P = \frac{dW}{dt}$.
$dW = \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}$.
$P = \vec{F} \cdot \frac{d\vec{r}}{dt}$.
Since $d\vec{r}/dt = \vec{v}$:
$P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v}$

related_concepts.name: Watt (W)
related_concepts.definition: SI unit of power ($1 J/s$). Horsepower ($1 HP = 746 W$).

subject: Physics
title: Work by Constant Force
description: Work done by a constant force over a straight displacement. \(F\)=force magnitude, \(d\)=displacement magnitude, \(\theta\)=angle between \(\vec{F}\) and \(\vec{d}\).

subject: Physics
title: Kinetic Energy
description: Energy of a body due to its motion. \(m\)=mass, \(v\)=speed, \(p=mv\)=linear momentum.

subject: Physics
title: Gravitational PE (near Earth)
description: Potential energy of a mass raised through small height near Earth's surface. \(m\)=mass, \(g\)=acceleration due to gravity, \(h\)=height above reference level.

subject: Physics
title: Force-PE Relation
description: Conservative force is the negative gradient of potential energy. \(F\)=force component, \(U\)=potential energy, \(x\)=position. (In 3D, \(\vec{F}=-\nabla U\).)

subject: Physics
title: Elastic PE of a Spring
description: Potential energy stored in a stretched/compressed spring. \(k\)=spring constant, \(x\)=deformation from natural length.
derivation:
Spring force \(F=-kx\)
Work done against spring \(=\int_0^x kx\,dx\)
\(U=\frac{1}{2}kx^2\)

subject: Physics
title: Conservation of Mechanical Energy
description: Total mechanical energy stays constant when only conservative forces act. \(K\)=kinetic energy, \(U\)=potential energy; subscripts \(i,f\)=initial, final states.

subject: Physics
title: Average Power
description: Rate of doing work over a time interval. \(W\)=total work done, \(t\)=time taken.

subject: Physics
title: Elastic Collision (1D) Final Velocities
description: Final velocities after a 1D perfectly elastic collision (momentum + KE conserved). \(m_1,m_2\)=masses, \(u_1,u_2\)=initial velocities, \(v_1,v_2\)=final velocities.

subject: Physics
title: Coefficient of Restitution
visual_data: e = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{u_1 - u_2} = \frac{\text{relative speed of separation}}{\text{relative speed of approach}}
description: Measures elasticity of a collision. \(e=1\) elastic, \(0<e<1\) inelastic, \(e=0\) perfectly inelastic. \(u\)=velocities before, \(v\)=velocities after.

subject: Physics
title: Perfectly Inelastic Collision (Common Velocity)
description: Bodies stick and move together after collision (momentum conserved, max KE loss). \(m_1,m_2\)=masses, \(u_1,u_2\)=initial velocities, \(v\)=common final velocity.

subject: Physics
title: KE Loss in Perfectly Inelastic Collision
description: Maximum kinetic energy lost when two bodies collide and stick. \(m_1,m_2\)=masses, \(u_1,u_2\)=initial velocities; the prefactor is the reduced mass.

subject: Physics
title: Elastic Collision: Equal Masses
visual_data: m_1 = m_2 \implies v_1 = u_2,\ v_2 = u_1
description: Standard result: in a 1D elastic collision of equal masses, the bodies exchange velocities. \(u\)=initial, \(v\)=final velocities.

subject: Physics
title: Work-Energy with Friction (Incline)
description: Net work on a block sliding distance \(s\) down a rough incline. \(h=s\sin\theta\)=height drop, \(\mu\)=friction coefficient, \(\theta\)=incline angle, \(s\)=path length.

subject: Physics
title: Vertical Circular Motion: Critical Speeds
description: Minimum speeds for a body in vertical circle (string/track) to complete the loop. \(g\)=gravity, \(R\)=radius. At top tension/normal force is zero; bottom value follows from energy conservation.
derivation:
At top: \(mg=\frac{mv_{top}^2}{R}\Rightarrow v_{top}=\sqrt{gR}\)
Energy conservation top to bottom: \(\frac{1}{2}v_{bottom}^2=\frac{1}{2}v_{top}^2+g(2R)\)
\(\Rightarrow v_{bottom}=\sqrt{5gR}\)

subject: Physics
title: Spring-Block Max Compression
description: Max compression when a moving block hits a spring on a smooth surface (energy conservation). \(m\)=mass, \(v\)=incoming speed, \(k\)=spring constant, \(x_{max}\)=maximum compression.

subject: Physics
title: Stable / Unstable Equilibrium
description: Equilibrium at PE extrema. Minimum of \(U\) (positive second derivative) is stable; maximum is unstable; zero second derivative is neutral. \(U\)=potential energy, \(x\)=position.

subject: Physics
title: Work by Spring Force
description: Work done by a spring as deformation changes (negative of PE change). \(k\)=spring constant, \(x_i,x_f\)=initial and final deformations from natural length.

subject: Physics
title: Mass-Energy Equivalence
description: Rest energy associated with mass (Einstein's relation, mentioned in NCERT energy discussion). \(m\)=mass, \(c\)=speed of light in vacuum.

subject: Physics
title: Momentum-Kinetic Energy Relations
description: Links momentum and kinetic energy of a single body. \(p\)=linear momentum, \(m\)=mass, \(K\)=kinetic energy. Useful when relating equal-KE or equal-momentum bodies.

subject: Physics
title: Coeff. of Restitution
description: Measure of elasticity of collision.
derivation:
Defined as ratio of relative speed after collision to relative speed before.
$v_{sep} = v_2 - v_1$ (Separation).
$v_{app} = u_1 - u_2$ (Approach).
Newton's Law of Impact states this ratio $e$ is constant for a material pair.

related_concepts.name: Elastic Collision
related_concepts.definition: Collision where Kinetic Energy is conserved ($e=1$).

related_concepts.name: Inelastic Collision
related_concepts.definition: Collision where KE is lost ($e < 1$). Perfectly inelastic ($e=0$) objects stick.

subject: Physics
title: CM Position (Discrete)
description: Coordinate of center of mass for particles.
derivation:
The Center of Mass is the unique point where the weighted relative position of the distributed mass sums to zero.
Defined such that the total moment of mass about the origin equals the sum of individual moments.
$M \vec{R}_{cm} = m_1 \vec{r}_1 + m_2 \vec{r}_2 + ...$

related_concepts.name: Conservation of Momentum
related_concepts.definition: If external force is zero, velocity of CM remains constant.

subject: Physics
title: CM: Semicircular Ring
description: Distance from center on symmetry axis.
derivation:
Orient ring in upper XY plane. By symmetry $X_{cm} = 0$.
Linear density $\lambda = M/(\pi R)$. Element $dm = \lambda (R d\theta)$.
Coordinate $y = R \sin \theta$.
$Y_{cm} = \frac{1}{M} \int y dm = \frac{1}{M} \int_0^\pi (R \sin \theta) (\frac{M}{\pi R} R d\theta)$.
$Y_{cm} = \frac{R}{\pi} \int_0^\pi \sin \theta d\theta = \frac{R}{\pi} [-\cos \theta]_0^\pi = \frac{2R}{\pi}$.

related_concepts.name: Line of Symmetry
related_concepts.definition: The CM always lies on the axis of symmetry if mass distribution is uniform.

subject: Physics
title: CM: Solid Hemisphere
description: Distance from base center.
derivation:
Slice into discs of radius $r = \sqrt{R^2-y^2}$ and thickness $dy$ at height $y$.
Volume of disc $dV = \pi (R^2-y^2) dy$.
Moment integration $\int y dV / \text{Volume}$.
$\int_0^R y \pi (R^2-y^2) dy = \pi [\frac{R^2 y^2}{2} - \frac{y^4}{4}]_0^R = \pi \frac{R^4}{4}$.
Total Volume $V = \frac{2}{3}\pi R^3$.
$Y_{cm} = \frac{\pi R^4 / 4}{2\pi R^3 / 3} = \frac{3R}{8}$.

related_concepts.name: Hollow Hemisphere
related_concepts.definition: For a hollow shell, $Y_{cm} = R/2$.

subject: Physics
title: Elastic Collision (1D)
description: Final velocity of mass $m_1$ after elastic head-on collision.
derivation:
Two conservation laws:
1. Momentum: $m_1 u_1 + m_2 u_2 = m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2$.
2. KE: $1/2 m_1 u_1^2 + ... = 1/2 m_1 v_1^2 + ...$
Or use Coeff of Restitution $e=1$: $v_2 - v_1 = u_1 - u_2$.
Solving linear equations yields the standard formula.

related_concepts.name: Mass Exchange
related_concepts.definition: If $m_1 = m_2$, velocities are exchanged ($v_1 = u_2, v_2 = u_1$).

subject: Physics
title: Inelastic Collision Loss
description: Loss in KE during head-on collision.
derivation:
Calculate $K_{initial} - K_{final}$.
Use conservation of momentum to find final velocities $v_1, v_2$ in terms of $e$.
Algebraic simplification yields the result.
Max loss for perfectly inelastic ($e=0$).
Zero loss for elastic ($e=1$).

related_concepts.name: Reduced Mass
related_concepts.definition: $\mu = \frac{m_1 m_2}{m_1+m_2}$. Simplifies two-body problems.

subject: Physics
title: CM Position (Continuous)
description: Centre of mass of a continuous body by integration. \(\vec{R}_{cm}\)=CM position, \(M\)=total mass, \(dm\)=mass element, \(\vec{r}\)=position of element.

subject: Physics
title: Velocity & Accel. of CM
description: Velocity and acceleration of centre of mass of a system. \(\vec{v}_{cm}\)=CM velocity, \(\vec{a}_{cm}\)=CM acceleration, \(m_i\)=mass of \(i\)-th particle, \(M\)=total mass.

subject: Physics
title: Newton's 2nd Law for System
description: Only external force accelerates the CM; internal forces cancel. \(\vec{F}_{ext}\)=net external force, \(M\)=total mass, \(\vec{a}_{cm}\)=CM acceleration, \(\vec{P}\)=total momentum.

subject: Physics
title: Conservation of Momentum
description: Total momentum is conserved when net external force is zero; CM moves at constant velocity. \(\vec{P}\)=total linear momentum, \(m_i,\vec{v}_i\)=mass and velocity of each particle.

subject: Physics
title: CM Shift (Internal Motion)
description: If no external force, CM stays fixed: displacements of two parts are oppositely directed and inversely proportional to mass (e.g. man-boat, recoil). \(m_i\)=mass, \(\Delta x_i\)=displacement of part \(i\).
derivation:
With \(F_{ext}=0\), CM does not move: \(\Delta X_{cm}=0\).
\(\frac{m_1\Delta x_1 + m_2\Delta x_2}{m_1+m_2}=0\)
\(\implies m_1\Delta x_1 = -m_2\Delta x_2\)

subject: Physics
title: Two-Particle Reduced Mass
description: Effective mass for relative motion of a two-body system; appears in collision energy-loss and relative-motion problems. \(\mu\)=reduced mass, \(m_1,m_2\)=the two masses.

subject: Physics
title: Elastic Collision: Final Speeds
description: Velocity of second body after 1D perfectly elastic collision (companion to \(v_1\)). \(v_2\)=final velocity of body 2, \(u_1,u_2\)=initial velocities, \(m_1,m_2\)=masses.

subject: Physics
title: Elastic Collision: Equal Masses
description: In a 1D elastic collision of equal masses, the bodies simply exchange velocities. \(u_1,u_2\)=initial velocities, \(v_1,v_2\)=final velocities.

subject: Physics
title: Elastic: Light Hits Heavy
description: Light body elastically striking a stationary very heavy body bounces back with same speed; heavy body stays nearly at rest. \(m_1\)=light mass, \(m_2\)=heavy mass, \(u_1\)=incoming speed.

subject: Physics
title: Elastic: Heavy Hits Light
description: Heavy body elastically striking a stationary light body keeps moving; light body shoots off at twice the speed. \(m_1\)=heavy mass, \(m_2\)=light mass, \(u_1\)=incoming speed.

subject: Physics
title: Perfectly Inelastic (Common Velocity)
description: Bodies stick together after a perfectly inelastic collision (\(e=0\)) and move with common velocity. \(v\)=common final velocity, \(m_i,u_i\)=masses and initial velocities.

subject: Physics
title: Velocities via Restitution
description: Final velocities for general 1D collision with restitution \(e\), from momentum conservation + \(v_{sep}=e\,v_{app}\). \(v_i\)=final, \(u_i\)=initial velocities, \(m_i\)=masses, \(e\)=coeff. of restitution.

subject: Physics
title: Max KE Loss in Collision
description: Maximum kinetic energy lost (perfectly inelastic, \(e=0\)); equals KE of relative motion. \(\mu=\frac{m_1m_2}{m_1+m_2}\)=reduced mass, \(u_1-u_2\)=approach velocity.

subject: Physics
title: Fractional KE Transfer (e=1)
description: Fraction of KE transferred from a moving body to a stationary one in a 1D elastic collision (max when \(m_1=m_2\)). \(K_1\)=initial KE of body 1, \(m_1,m_2\)=masses.

subject: Physics
title: Height After Each Bounce
description: Rebound height of a ball dropped from \(h_0\) after \(n\) bounces off the floor. \(h_n\)=height after \(n\)th bounce, \(e\)=coeff. of restitution, \(h_0\)=initial drop height.
derivation:
Speed just before hitting: \(v=\sqrt{2gh_0}\); after bounce \(v'=ev\).
Rebound height \(h_1=\frac{v'^2}{2g}=e^2 h_0\).
Repeating \(n\) times: \(h_n=e^{2n}h_0\).

subject: Physics
title: Total Distance (Bouncing Ball)
description: Total path length travelled by a ball dropped from \(h_0\) until it stops bouncing. \(H\)=total distance, \(e\)=coeff. of restitution, \(h_0\)=initial height.

subject: Physics
title: Total Time (Bouncing Ball)
description: Total time a ball bounces before coming to rest, dropped from height \(h_0\). \(T\)=total time, \(e\)=coeff. of restitution, \(g\)=gravity, \(h_0\)=initial height.

subject: Physics
title: Oblique Elastic (Equal Mass)
description: When a moving body elastically collides obliquely with an identical stationary body, the two move off at right angles. \(\theta_1,\theta_2\)=angles of the two bodies with the original line of motion.

subject: Physics
title: Oblique Collision Components
description: In oblique collision, restitution acts only along the line of impact (normal); the tangential velocity component is unchanged. \(\perp\)=along line of impact (normal), \(\parallel\)=tangential, \(e\)=coeff. of restitution.

subject: Physics
title: Impulse–Momentum Theorem
description: Impulse of a force equals the change in momentum it produces; used in collisions/short-duration forces. \(\vec{J}\)=impulse, \(\vec{F}\)=force, \(\Delta\vec{p}\)=change in momentum.

subject: Physics
title: Variable Mass / Rocket Eqn.
description: Thrust equation for a body gaining/losing mass (rocket). \(M\)=instantaneous mass, \(v_{rel}\)=exhaust speed relative to body, \(\frac{dM}{dt}\)=rate of mass loss, \(F_{ext}\)=external force.

subject: Physics
title: Rocket Velocity (Tsiolkovsky)
description: Speed of a rocket against gravity after burning fuel. \(u\)=initial speed, \(v_{rel}\)=exhaust speed, \(M_0\)=initial mass, \(M\)=mass at time \(t\), \(g\)=gravity.

subject: Physics
title: CM: Triangular Plate
description: CM of a uniform triangular lamina lies at its centroid, at one-third of any median's length from the base. \(h\)=height (perpendicular distance from base to opposite vertex).

subject: Physics
title: CM: Solid/Hollow Cone (Summary)
description: CM heights of a uniform cone from the base: solid vs hollow (lateral surface). \(h\)=height of cone, measured along axis from base.

subject: Physics
title: CM: Circular Arc (Wire)
description: CM of a uniform circular arc of half-angle \(\theta\), measured from the centre along the bisector (full angle \(2\theta\) in radians). \(R\)=radius, \(\theta\)=half the arc's subtended angle.

subject: Physics
title: CM by Cavity (Negative Mass)
description: CM of a body with a cut-out cavity: treat removed part as negative mass. \(m_1,\vec{r}_1\)=full body, \(m_2,\vec{r}_2\)=removed (cavity) part with its own CM.

subject: Physics
title: KE in Terms of Momentum
description: Kinetic energy expressed via momentum; handy in collision/momentum problems. \(K\)=kinetic energy, \(p\)=momentum magnitude, \(m\)=mass.

subject: Physics
title: Heat Conduction
description: Rate of heat flow.
derivation:
Fourier's Law of Conduction.
Heat current $H$ is proportional to Area $A$ and Temp gradient $-dT/dx$.
$H = -KA \frac{dT}{dx}$.
For steady state rod of length $l$: $-dT/dx = (T_1 - T_2)/l$.
$H = \frac{KA \Delta T}{l}$

related_concepts.name: Thermal Conductivity
related_concepts.definition: Material property $K$ indicating ability to conduct heat.

subject: Physics
title: Thermal Resistance
description: Analogy to electrical resistance.
derivation:
Compare heat flow equation to Ohm's Law $I = V/R$.
Heat Current $H = \frac{\Delta T}{l/KA}$.
Temperature Difference $\Delta T$ is analogous to Potential Diff $V$.
Therefore, $R_{th} = \frac{l}{KA}$.

related_concepts.name: Series Combination
related_concepts.definition: Resistances add up ($R_{eq} = R_1 + R_2$) when heat flows through slabs sequentially.

subject: Physics
title: Stefan-Boltzmann Law
description: Power radiated by a body.
derivation:
Empirical law derived by Stefan and Boltzmann.
Energy radiated per second per unit area of a black body is $\propto T^4$.
$P_{black} = \sigma A T^4$.
For gray body, multiply by emissivity $e$ ($0 < e < 1$).

related_concepts.name: Black Body
related_concepts.definition: Ideal absorber and emitter ($e=1$).

subject: Physics
title: Wien's Displacement Law
description: Peak wavelength vs Temperature.
derivation:
Observed from Black Body Radiation spectrum.
The wavelength $\lambda_m$ corresponding to max intensity shifts to lower values as $T$ increases.
$\lambda_m \propto 1/T$.
$b$ is Wien's constant.

related_concepts.name: Color of Stars
related_concepts.definition: Hotter stars appear blue (lower $\lambda$), cooler stars appear red.

subject: Physics
title: Newton's Law of Cooling
description: Cooling rate for small temp difference.
derivation:
Approximation of Stefan's Law for small $\Delta T$.
Rate of loss $R \propto (T^4 - T_s^4)$.
If $T = T_s + \Delta T$, then $T^4 \approx T_s^4 (1 + 4\Delta T/T_s)$.
$R \propto \Delta T \propto (T - T_s)$.
$\frac{dT}{dt} = -K(T - T_s)$

related_concepts.name: Exponential Decay
related_concepts.definition: Temperature excess decays exponentially with time.

subject: Physics
title: Linear Expansion
description: Thermal expansion of solids.
derivation:
Experimental observation for small $\Delta T$.
Change in length is proportional to original length and temp change.
$\Delta L \propto L$ and $\Delta L \propto \Delta T$.
Constant of proportionality is $\alpha$.

related_concepts.name: Areal/Volume Expansion
related_concepts.definition: $\beta = 2\alpha$ (Area) and $\gamma = 3\alpha$ (Volume) for isotropic solids.

subject: Physics
title: Calorimetry Principle
description: Heat Lost = Heat Gained.
derivation:
Based on Law of Conservation of Energy.
In an isolated system, total energy is constant.
Heat lost by hot body = Heat gained by cold body.
$Q_{lost} = m_1 s_1 (T_1 - T)$
$Q_{gained} = m_2 s_2 (T - T_2)$
Equating them gives the equilibrium temperature $T$.

related_concepts.name: Specific Heat Capacity
related_concepts.definition: Heat required to raise temp of 1kg substance by 1°C ($s$).

related_concepts.name: Water Equivalent
related_concepts.definition: Mass of water that would absorb the same heat as the given body for the same temp rise.

subject: Physics
title: Composite Slab (Series)
description: Equivalent thermal resistance.
derivation:
In series, Heat Current $H$ is constant.
Temp drop $\Delta T = \Delta T_1 + \Delta T_2$.
Using $\Delta T = H R_{th}$:
$H R_{eq} = H R_1 + H R_2$.
$R_{eq} = R_1 + R_2$.
where $R = l/KA$.

related_concepts.name: Steady State
related_concepts.definition: Condition where temperature at any point does not change with time.

subject: Physics
title: Composite Slab (Series)
description: Equivalent thermal resistance. Heat current is same.
derivation:
In series, Heat Current $H$ is constant through both slabs.
Temperature drop $\Delta T = \Delta T_1 + \Delta T_2$.
Using $\Delta T = H R_{th}$:
$H R_{eq} = H R_1 + H R_2$.
$R_{eq} = R_1 + R_2$.

related_concepts.name: Steady State
related_concepts.definition: The condition where the temperature at any point in the material does not change with time.

subject: Physics
title: Composite Slab (Parallel)
description: Equivalent thermal resistance. Temperature difference is same.
derivation:
In parallel, Temperature difference $\Delta T$ is the same for both slabs.
Total Heat Current $H = H_1 + H_2$.
$\frac{\Delta T}{R_{eq}} = \frac{\Delta T}{R_1} + \frac{\Delta T}{R_2}$.
$\frac{1}{R_{eq}} = \frac{1}{R_1} + \frac{1}{R_2}$.

related_concepts.name: Equivalent Conductivity
related_concepts.definition: $K_{eq} = \frac{K_1 A_1 + K_2 A_2}{A_1 + A_2}$ for parallel slabs of same length.

subject: Physics
title: Junction Temperature
description: Temp at interface of two slabs in series.
derivation:
At steady state, heat flow from Slab 1 = Heat flow into Slab 2.
$H_1 = H_2$.
$\frac{K_1 A (T_1 - T)}{l_1} = \frac{K_2 A (T - T_2)}{l_2}$.
Rearrange to solve for $T$:
$K_1 l_2 (T_1 - T) = K_2 l_1 (T - T_2)$.
$T(K_1 l_2 + K_2 l_1) = K_1 l_2 T_1 + K_2 l_1 T_2$.

related_concepts.name: Thermal Gradient
related_concepts.definition: The rate of temperature change with distance ($dT/dx$). Constant in steady state uniform conduction.

subject: Physics
title: Temperature Scale Conversion
description: Converts between Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales. \(C\)=Celsius, \(F\)=Fahrenheit, \(K\)=Kelvin (absolute).

subject: Physics
title: General Thermometric Relation
description: Temperature on Celsius scale from any thermometric property \(X\). \(X\)=property at temperature \(t\), \(X_0\)=value at ice point, \(X_{100}\)=value at steam point.

subject: Physics
title: Area Expansion
description: Increase in area of a solid on heating. \(\Delta A\)=change in area, \(A\)=original area, \(\beta\)=coefficient of superficial (area) expansion, \(\Delta T\)=temperature rise.

subject: Physics
title: Volume Expansion
description: Increase in volume of a solid/liquid on heating. \(\Delta V\)=change in volume, \(V\)=original volume, \(\gamma\)=coefficient of cubical (volume) expansion, \(\Delta T\)=temperature rise.

subject: Physics
title: Relation Between Expansion Coefficients
description: For an isotropic solid, the three expansion coefficients are in ratio 1:2:3. \(\alpha\)=linear, \(\beta\)=area (superficial), \(\gamma\)=volume (cubical) coefficient.

subject: Physics
title: Thermal Stress
description: Stress developed in a rod rigidly clamped at both ends and heated/cooled (length fixed). \(F/A\)=thermal stress, \(Y\)=Young's modulus, \(\alpha\)=linear expansion coefficient, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change.
derivation:
Free expansion strain \(=\alpha \Delta T\).
Clamps prevent it, producing equal compressive strain.
Stress \(= Y \times\) strain \(= Y \alpha \Delta T\).

subject: Physics
title: Thermal Force on Clamped Rod
description: Total force exerted by a clamped rod on supports when temperature changes. \(F\)=force, \(Y\)=Young's modulus, \(A\)=cross-sectional area, \(\alpha\)=linear expansion coefficient, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change.

subject: Physics
title: Variation of Density with Temperature
description: Density of a substance decreases on heating. \(\rho\)=density at higher temperature, \(\rho_0\)=initial density, \(\gamma\)=cubical expansion coefficient, \(\Delta T\)=temperature rise.

subject: Physics
title: Apparent & Real Expansion of Liquid
description: Observed (apparent) liquid expansion is reduced by expansion of the container. \(\gamma_{real}\)=real (absolute) expansion coefficient of liquid, \(\gamma_{app}\)=apparent expansion coefficient, \(\gamma_{vessel}\)=cubical expansion coefficient of vessel \((=3\alpha)\).

subject: Physics
title: Pendulum Clock Time Error
description: Fractional change in time period of a pendulum clock with temperature (loss/gain per unit time). \(\Delta T/T\)=fractional change in period, \(\alpha\)=linear expansion coefficient of pendulum, \(\Delta\theta\)=temperature change.
derivation:
\(T = 2\pi \sqrt{L/g}\Rightarrow T \propto L^{1/2}\).
\(\frac{\Delta T}{T} = \frac{1}{2}\frac{\Delta L}{L} = \frac{1}{2}\alpha\Delta\theta\).

subject: Physics
title: Scale Reading Error (Thermal)
description: True length when a metal scale calibrated at one temperature is used at another. \(L_{true}\)=actual length, \(L_{read}\)=scale reading, \(\alpha\)=linear expansion coefficient of scale, \(\Delta T\)=temperature above calibration.

subject: Physics
title: Heat Absorbed (Sensible Heat)
description: Heat needed to change temperature of a body without phase change. \(Q\)=heat, \(m\)=mass, \(s\)=specific heat capacity, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change.

subject: Physics
title: Latent Heat
description: Heat exchanged during a phase change at constant temperature. \(Q\)=heat, \(m\)=mass undergoing phase change, \(L\)=specific latent heat (fusion \(L_f\) or vaporization \(L_v\)).

subject: Physics
title: Heat Capacity & Water Equivalent
description: Heat capacity of a body and its water equivalent. \(C\)=heat capacity, \(m\)=mass, \(s\)=specific heat, \(W\)=water equivalent (mass of water needing same heat), \(s_w\)=specific heat of water.

subject: Physics
title: Molar Heat Capacity
description: Heat per mole per degree rise. \(C\)=molar heat capacity, \(M\)=molar mass, \(s\)=specific heat, \(Q\)=heat, \(n\)=moles, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change.

subject: Physics
title: Newton's Cooling (Average Form)
description: Practical (finite-interval) form of Newton's law of cooling for problem solving. \(T_1,T_2\)=initial and final body temperatures, \(t\)=time, \(T_s\)=surroundings temperature, \(K\)=cooling constant.

subject: Physics
title: Newton's Cooling (Exponential)
