description: Fictitious force in an accelerating (non-inertial) frame, opposite to frame acceleration. \(m\)=mass of body, \(\vec{a}_{frame}\)=acceleration of the reference frame.

subject: Physics
title: Minimum Force to Pull Block (Optimum Angle)
description: Least force to drag a block on a rough surface, applied at the optimum angle. \(\mu\)=friction coefficient, \(m\)=mass, \(g\)=gravity, \(\theta\)=angle of pull above horizontal.

subject: Physics
title: First Law of Thermodynamics
description: Conservation of energy for thermodynamic systems.
derivation:
Heat supplied to a system ($\Delta Q$) is used in two ways:
1. To increase Internal Energy ($\Delta U$, temperature rise).
2. To do Work against external pressure ($\Delta W$, expansion).
Note: Sign convention is crucial (Work done BY system is +ve).

related_concepts.name: State Function
related_concepts.definition: A property whose value does not depend on the path taken (e.g., Internal Energy $U$).

subject: Physics
title: Mayer's Relation
description: Relates molar heat capacities for ideal gas.
derivation:
Enthalpy $H = U + PV = U + RT$ (for 1 mole).
Differentiate w.r.t $T$: $\frac{dH}{dT} = \frac{dU}{dT} + R$.
By definition, $C_p = \frac{dH}{dT}$ and $C_v = \frac{dU}{dT}$.
Therefore, $C_p = C_v + R$.

related_concepts.name: Universal Gas Constant
related_concepts.definition: $R \approx 8.314$ J/(mol K).

subject: Physics
title: Work Done (Isothermal)
description: Work done at constant temperature ($PV = \text{const}$).
derivation:
$W = \int_{V_1}^{V_2} P dV$.
For ideal gas, $P = nRT/V$.
$W = \int_{V_1}^{V_2} \frac{nRT}{V} dV = nRT \int \frac{dV}{V}$.
$W = nRT [\ln V]_{V_1}^{V_2} = nRT \ln(V_2/V_1)$.

related_concepts.name: Boyle's Law
related_concepts.definition: For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume.

subject: Physics
title: Work Done (Adiabatic)
description: Work done with no heat exchange ($PV^\gamma = \text{const}$).
derivation:
$P = K V^{-\gamma}$.
$W = \int K V^{-\gamma} dV = K [\frac{V^{1-\gamma}}{1-\gamma}]_{V_1}^{V_2}$.
$W = \frac{K V_2^{1-\gamma} - K V_1^{1-\gamma}}{1-\gamma}$.
Since $K = P_1 V_1^\gamma = P_2 V_2^\gamma$:
$W = \frac{P_2 V_2 - P_1 V_1}{1-\gamma} = \frac{P_1 V_1 - P_2 V_2}{\gamma - 1}$.

related_concepts.name: Adiabatic Index
related_concepts.definition: $\gamma = C_p/C_v$. Always greater than 1.

subject: Physics
title: Carnot Efficiency
description: Max efficiency of heat engine. $T_1$: Source, $T_2$: Sink (Kelvin).
derivation:
Efficiency $\eta = \frac{\text{Work Output}}{\text{Heat Input}} = \frac{Q_1 - Q_2}{Q_1} = 1 - \frac{Q_2}{Q_1}$.
For a reversible Carnot cycle, heat transfer is proportional to temperature ($Q \propto T$).
$\frac{Q_2}{Q_1} = \frac{T_2}{T_1}$.
$\eta = 1 - \frac{T_2}{T_1}$.

related_concepts.name: Second Law of Thermodynamics
related_concepts.definition: No heat engine can have 100% efficiency (Kelvin-Planck statement).

subject: Physics
title: Entropy Change
description: Measure of disorder. State function.
derivation:
For reversible process, $dS = dQ/T$.
1. Isothermal ($T$ const): $\Delta S = Q/T$.
2. Phase Change: $\Delta S = mL/T$.
3. Adiabatic ($dQ=0$): $\Delta S = 0$ (Isentropic).
For Ideal Gas: $\Delta S = nC_v \ln(T_2/T_1) + nR \ln(V_2/V_1)$.

related_concepts.name: Second Law
related_concepts.definition: Total entropy of an isolated system always increases ($\Delta S_{univ} \ge 0$).

subject: Physics
title: Polytropic Process Work
description: Work done in process $PV^n = \text{constant}$.
derivation:
Similar to Adiabatic ($n = \gamma$) derivation.
$W = \int_{V_1}^{V_2} \frac{C}{V^n} dV = C [\frac{V^{1-n}}{1-n}]_{V_1}^{V_2}$.
$W = \frac{C V_2^{1-n} - C V_1^{1-n}}{1-n}$.
Substitute $C = P_1 V_1^n = P_2 V_2^n$:
$W = \frac{P_2 V_2 - P_1 V_1}{1-n} = \frac{P_1 V_1 - P_2 V_2}{n-1}$.

related_concepts.name: Molar Heat Capacity
related_concepts.definition: For polytropic process: $C = C_v + \frac{R}{1-n}$.

subject: Physics
title: Work Done = Area under PV Curve
description: Work done by a gas in any quasi-static process equals area under the P-V curve. \(W\)=work by gas, \(P\)=pressure, \(dV\)=small volume change. Positive on expansion, negative on compression.

subject: Physics
title: Work Done (Isobaric)
visual_data: W = P \Delta V = nR \Delta T = nR(T_2 - T_1)
description: Work done by gas at constant pressure. \(W\)=work, \(P\)=pressure, \(\Delta V\)=volume change, \(n\)=moles, \(R\)=gas constant, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change.

subject: Physics
title: Work Done (Isochoric)
description: At constant volume no work is done, so all heat raises internal energy. \(W\)=work, \(\Delta Q\)=heat, \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change, \(n\)=moles, \(C_v\)=molar heat capacity at constant volume.

subject: Physics
title: Internal Energy of Ideal Gas
description: Internal energy change of an ideal gas depends only on temperature (state function), valid for ALL processes. \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change, \(n\)=moles, \(C_v\)=molar heat at constant volume, \(f\)=degrees of freedom, \(R\)=gas constant, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change.

subject: Physics
title: Molar Heat Capacities (Degrees of Freedom)
description: Molar specific heats and ratio in terms of degrees of freedom. \(C_v\)=molar heat at constant volume, \(C_p\)=molar heat at constant pressure, \(f\)=degrees of freedom, \(R\)=gas constant, \(\gamma\)=adiabatic ratio.

subject: Physics
title: Adiabatic Relations (Poisson)
description: Pressure-volume-temperature relations for a reversible adiabatic (no heat exchange) process. \(P\)=pressure, \(V\)=volume, \(T\)=temperature, \(\gamma=C_p/C_v\).

subject: Physics
title: Molar Heat Capacity (Polytropic)
description: Effective molar heat capacity for a polytropic process \(PV^n=\)const. \(C\)=molar heat capacity, \(C_v\)=heat at constant volume, \(R\)=gas constant, \(n\)=polytropic index, \(\gamma\)=adiabatic ratio.

subject: Physics
title: Slope of Adiabat vs Isotherm
description: On a P-V diagram the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isotherm by factor \(\gamma\). \(P\)=pressure, \(V\)=volume, \(\gamma=C_p/C_v\). Isothermal slope \(=-P/V\), adiabatic slope \(=-\gamma P/V\).

subject: Physics
title: Mixture of Gases (Effective Cv)
description: Effective molar heat capacity of a non-reacting gas mixture. \(n_1,n_2\)=moles, \(C_{v_1},C_{v_2}\)=molar heats at constant volume, \(C_{p,mix}=C_{v,mix}+R\), \(\gamma_{mix}\)=effective ratio.

subject: Physics
title: Refrigerator / AC Coefficient of Performance
description: Performance of a refrigerator (last expression for a Carnot refrigerator). \(\beta\)=COP, \(Q_2\)=heat extracted from cold body, \(Q_1\)=heat rejected to hot, \(W\)=work input, \(T_1,T_2\)=hot/cold reservoir temperatures (Kelvin).

subject: Physics
title: Heat Pump Coefficient of Performance
description: Performance of a heat pump (heating mode). \(Q_1\)=heat delivered to hot body, \(W\)=work input, \(T_1,T_2\)=hot/cold temperatures (Kelvin), \(\beta_{ref}\)=refrigerator COP.

subject: Physics
title: Efficiency (General Heat Engine)
description: Efficiency of any heat engine in one cycle. \(\eta\)=efficiency, \(W\)=net work output, \(Q_1\)=heat absorbed from source, \(Q_2\)=heat rejected to sink.

subject: Physics
title: Cyclic Process Results
description: Over a complete cycle internal energy is unchanged, so net heat equals net work (area enclosed on P-V diagram). Clockwise loop: positive work (engine); anticlockwise: negative.

subject: Physics
title: Free Expansion (Joule Expansion)
description: Adiabatic expansion of ideal gas into vacuum: no heat, no work, no temperature change. \(\Delta Q\)=heat, \(\Delta W\)=work, \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change, \(T\)=temperature. Irreversible process.

subject: Physics
title: Carnot Cycle Heat Ratio
description: For a reversible Carnot engine the ratio of heats exchanged equals the ratio of reservoir temperatures. \(Q_1\)=heat absorbed at source, \(Q_2\)=heat rejected at sink, \(T_1,T_2\)=source/sink temperatures (Kelvin).

subject: Physics
title: Heat Added (Isothermal = Work)
description: In an isothermal process internal energy is constant, so all heat absorbed converts to work. \(\Delta Q\)=heat, \(\Delta W\)=work, \(n\)=moles, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature, \(V_1,V_2\)=initial/final volume.

subject: Physics
title: Specific Heat Relation (cp - cv)
description: Mayer relation in specific (per kg) and molar forms. \(c_p,c_v\)=specific heats per unit mass, \(C_p,C_v\)=molar specific heats, \(R\)=gas constant, \(M\)=molar mass.

subject: Physics
title: Entropy Change (Ideal Gas)
description: Entropy change of an ideal gas between two states (state function). \(\Delta S\)=entropy change, \(n\)=moles, \(C_v\)=molar heat at constant volume, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T_1,T_2\)=temperatures, \(V_1,V_2\)=volumes.
